title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a broader framework for nonequilibrium work relations.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is a cornerstone of nonequilibrium thermodynamics, but its inequality form has been less explored; the authors aim to extend it to more complex systems including dissipative and field-theoretic contexts.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using path integral methods and fluctuation theorems, incorporating dissipation and field-theoretic degrees of freedom.
result: They obtain new inequalities that relate work distributions to free energy differences in systems with dissipation and fields, showing that the standard inequality is a special case.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities provide a more complete thermodynamic description for a wider class of nonequilibrium processes, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and statistical mechanics.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases that are not well understood experimentally.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting processor, the authors implement a quantum circuit with repeated measurements and conditional feedback, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement entropy.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, controlled by the measurement rate and feedback strength, consistent with theoretical predictions for monitored quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used to engineer nonequilibrium phases of matter, providing a platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and information processing in open systems.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in classical systems; its quantum counterpart is of fundamental interest in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states at different effective temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics under controlled dissipation.
result: They observe the quantum Mpemba effect, where initially hotter states relax faster, and demonstrate modulation of the effect by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of the quantum Mpemba effect, opening avenues for controlling relaxation dynamics in quantum systems and testing thermodynamic bounds.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle flows and fluctuations in driven dissipative quantum systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, but existing methods treat dissipation and driving separately.
method: The authors develop a diagrammatic perturbation theory within the Keldysh-Lindblad framework, introducing dissipative interaction lines to represent quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute nonequilibrium steady states and response functions for open quantum systems with strong correlations and driving.
conclusion: This work advances the theoretical toolkit for analyzing quantum thermodynamic processes in realistic open systems, with implications for quantum heat engines and information processing.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Relaxation And Quantum Mpemba Effect In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Emerson Lima Caldas And Diego Paiva Pires
abstract:
Author(s): Emerson Lima Caldas and Diego Paiva Pires

The Mpemba effect happens when a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster than a system closer to equilibrium. The authors study the relaxation of systems whose effective dynamics are described by Davies maps, providing a framework to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect in Markovian open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012418] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems described by Davies maps, showing that systems initially further from equilibrium can relax faster than those closer to equilibrium.
motivation: The Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster. Understanding this effect in quantum systems could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors consider Markovian open quantum systems governed by Davies maps and derive conditions under which the quantum Mpemba effect occurs. They provide a framework to engineer this effect by tuning system parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect can be exponentially accelerated, meaning the relaxation time difference can be made arbitrarily large by appropriate parameter choices.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems, which may be useful for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Entanglement Recovery By Reversing The Effect Of Noise In A Quantum Repeater
authors: Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, And Seung-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, and Seung-Woo Lee

We propose a method to directly recover the degree of entanglement distributed by entanglement swapping in the presence of noise. Our approach introduces a reversing operation that probabilistically undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012602] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a reversing operation to recover entanglement degraded by amplitude damping or photon loss in quantum repeaters.
motivation: Entanglement swapping in quantum repeaters suffers from noise, reducing the fidelity of distributed entanglement. Existing methods require multiple copies or complex distillation; a direct recovery method is needed.
method: Introduces a probabilistic reversing operation that undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded recovery of entanglement after swapping.
result: The reversing operation can restore the degree of entanglement to near-ideal levels with a certain success probability, improving the performance of quantum repeater networks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for mitigating noise in quantum repeaters, enhancing the feasibility of long-distance quantum communication.

title: Quantum Strategies To Overcome Classical Multiplexing Limits
authors: Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, And Stephanie D. C. Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, and Stephanie D. C. Wehner

Near-term quantum networks face a bottleneck due to low quantum communication rates. This degrades performance both by lowering operating speeds and increasing qubit storage time in noisy memories, making some quantum internet applications infeasible. One way to circumvent this bottleneck is multipl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012603] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes quantum strategies to overcome classical multiplexing limits in near-term quantum networks, improving communication rates.
motivation: Near-term quantum networks suffer from low communication rates, which degrade performance and make some quantum internet applications infeasible. Classical multiplexing cannot fully address this bottleneck.
method: The authors develop quantum multiplexing strategies that exploit quantum properties to increase the effective communication rate, and analyze their performance under realistic noise and memory constraints.
result: The proposed quantum strategies significantly outperform classical multiplexing, enabling higher rates and reducing qubit storage time in noisy memories.
conclusion: Quantum multiplexing offers a practical way to enhance near-term quantum network performance, bringing quantum internet applications closer to feasibility.

title: Consistent Monitoring Of Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

This Letter considers whether fluctuations of extensive quantities in many-body systems can be consistently monitored, namely, whether measurements can be performed without disturbing future outcome distribution. The answer turns out to be “no” in a large class of situations, and the amount of disturbance can be exactly calculated in terms of linear response quantities.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates whether fluctuations of extensive quantities in many-body systems can be monitored without disturbing future outcome distributions, finding that such consistent monitoring is generally impossible and quantifying the disturbance.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of measuring fluctuations in quantum many-body systems is crucial for thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The author uses linear response theory to calculate the disturbance caused by measurements on the future distribution of fluctuations.
result: Consistent monitoring is impossible in a large class of situations, and the disturbance can be exactly expressed in terms of linear response quantities.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental trade-off between measurement and disturbance in quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and metrology.

title: Bundling Of Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, and Wolfgang Lechner

We investigate bipartite entanglement and prove that in constrained energy subspaces, the entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are the same across the whole subspace. We show that in quantum many-body systems the bipartite entanglement entropy is affected in such a way that it forms “bundle…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that in constrained energy subspaces, entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are identical, leading to 'bundles' of bipartite entanglement.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in many-body systems is crucial, but computing it for all bipartitions is costly. The authors aim to identify constraints that simplify entanglement structure.
method: They analyze bipartite entanglement in constrained energy subspaces of quantum many-body systems, proving that entanglement spectra for multiple bipartitions coincide across the subspace.
result: Entanglement spectra form bundles, implying that bipartite entanglement entropy is uniform across certain bipartitions within the subspace.
conclusion: This bundling effect reduces the complexity of characterizing entanglement in many-body systems and may aid in quantum information tasks.

title: Quantifying And Probing Multipartite Entanglement Via Minimum Entanglement Drop
authors: Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, and Dong Wang

Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement remains a significant challenge due to the exponential scaling of computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a multipartite entanglement monotone defined by the minimum entanglement drop—the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a multipartite entanglement monotone based on minimum entanglement drop, providing a computable measure for genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging due to exponential complexity; existing measures are often hard to compute.
method: Defines the minimum entanglement drop as the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a single particle is discarded, and proves it is an entanglement monotone.
result: The measure is shown to be monotonic under local operations and classical communication, and is computable for various multipartite states.
conclusion: The minimum entanglement drop offers a practical and theoretically sound way to quantify genuine multipartite entanglement.

title: Quantitative And Optimal Device-independent Lower Bounds On Detection Efficiency
authors: Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, And Peter Bierhorst
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, and Peter Bierhorst

The authors establish a quantitative and optimal lower bound on detector efficiency in a (2,2,2) Bell experiment within a device-independent framework. They provide a tight lower bound on the minimum efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation using the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012404] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes quantitative and optimal device-independent lower bounds on detection efficiency for Bell-CHSH violations.
motivation: Device-independent protocols require minimal detection efficiency to close the detection loophole; prior bounds were not tight or optimal.
method: Uses the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to derive tight lower bounds on detector efficiency in a (2,2,2) Bell scenario.
result: Provides a tight, optimal lower bound on the minimum detection efficiency needed to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation.
conclusion: The bounds are optimal and can guide experimental implementations of device-independent protocols.

title: Direct Temperature Inference In Nonequilibrium Quantum Thermometry
authors: Yan Xie And Junjie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Xie and Junjie Liu

Quantum thermometry aims to measure temperature in nanoscale quantum systems, paralleling classical thermometry. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, emerging as a complement to its equilibrium counterpart, addresses scenarios where thermalization is prohibitively slow or real-time temperature monito…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062226] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a direct temperature inference method for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, bypassing the need for thermalization.
motivation: Traditional quantum thermometry relies on thermalization, which can be slow or impractical; nonequilibrium methods are needed for real-time monitoring.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using quantum probes and measurement strategies to infer temperature directly from nonequilibrium dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that temperature can be accurately estimated even when the probe is not in thermal equilibrium, with bounds on precision.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to quantum thermometry in nonequilibrium settings, relevant for nanoscale thermal management.

title: Efficient Quantum Thermal State Preparation Via Local Driving: Lindbladian Simulation With Provable Guarantees
authors: Dominik Hahn, S. A. Parameswaran, And Benedikt Placke
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, S. A. Parameswaran, and Benedikt Placke

Preparing the thermal density matrix [MATH] corresponding to a given Hamiltonian [MATH] is a task of central interest across quantum many-body physics, and is particularly salient when attempting to study it with quantum computers. Although solved in principle by recent constructions of ef…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient algorithm for preparing thermal states of quantum many-body systems using local Lindbladian dynamics with provable guarantees.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for studying quantum many-body physics, but existing methods are often inefficient or lack rigorous guarantees.
method: The authors design a local Lindbladian evolution that drives the system to the desired thermal state, leveraging the concept of thermalization and providing bounds on the mixing time.
result: They prove that the algorithm prepares thermal states in polynomial time for a class of Hamiltonians, with explicit bounds on the error and resource requirements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and provably efficient approach to thermal state preparation, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations via thermodynamic length in far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking; the paper aims to connect fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations through thermodynamic length.
method: Derives a general expression for thermodynamic length in stochastic thermodynamics and shows how it relates to both fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
result: Establishes a unified perspective linking thermodynamic length, fluctuation relations, and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, providing new bounds on current fluctuations.
conclusion: Thermodynamic length serves as a unifying concept in stochastic thermodynamics, offering deeper insight into far-from-equilibrium processes.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects play a significant role.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator, analyzing fluctuations and efficiency.
result: They derive exact expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and a trade-off between power and efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive thermodynamic analysis of a quantum resonator, highlighting the impact of quantum coherence on heat-to-work conversion.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly improve entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential advantage, but their impact on repeater protocols needs systematic study.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters using multimode sources, considering realistic noise and loss. They analyze the entanglement generation rate and fidelity as functions of the number of modes and other parameters.
result: Multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity. The optimal number of modes depends on the specific repeater architecture and noise levels.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, bringing practical long-distance quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, and nonreciprocal elements offer a way to control the flow of quantum correlations.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to generate remote entanglement. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond are promising but achieving above-unity cooperativity has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and coupled individual tin-vacancy centers to them. Measured the coherent cooperativity via resonant reflection spectroscopy and second-order correlation measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding 1, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which enables high-fidelity entanglement generation between distant nodes.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities as a viable platform for quantum network nodes, paving the way for scalable entanglement distribution.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir to create and stabilize multipartite entangled states, with reconfigurable coupling via external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate robust entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and can be used to engineer topological many-body states, with high fidelity and resilience to noise.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for scalable entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors; passive schemes could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive error correction code that protects against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, demonstrating that passive error correction can outperform the physical qubit.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the polynomial scaling without recording. This demonstrates a measurement-induced phase transition in information lifetime.
conclusion: Recording midcircuit measurements provides a powerful strategy to protect quantum information, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on non-classical resources, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the experimental demonstration confirms the presence of non-projective measurements in a trapped-ion system.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for certifying non-projective measurements, advancing quantum information processing and device-independent protocols.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy in a minimal detector model.
method: The authors model a quantum particle detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using a master equation approach. They derive bounds relating entropy production to measurement accuracy.
result: They find that higher measurement accuracy inevitably leads to greater entropy production, establishing a fundamental thermodynamic cost for information acquisition. The trade-off is quantified by a bound that depends on detector parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational understanding of the thermodynamics of quantum measurement, with implications for designing energy-efficient quantum sensors and detectors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and coherence times under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures and using specific cavity designs can significantly improve spectral stability.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, provided that charge noise is minimized through proper material engineering and operating conditions.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging programmable quantum matter concepts.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with low overhead, scalable to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward large-scale quantum networks using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics using stabilizer codes and random measurement protocols, deriving conditions for successful decoding based on measurement statistics.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they characterize the stability of logical information under partial measurement.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, offering new insights into the interplay between measurements and code performance.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, achieving miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize a compact, scalable quantum random number generator with device-independent security guarantees, addressing the need for practical quantum cryptography hardware.
method: Implements a self-testing protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction, with real-time parameter estimation.
result: Achieves high-speed randomness generation with provable security based on Bell inequality violation, all on a single photonic chip.
conclusion: The work paves the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion onto a photonic platform.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols are resource-intensive and sensitive to losses. The authors aim to enhance near-term feasibility.
method: They introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the required number of emitters and improve the loss tolerance of quantum repeater protocols, making them more practical.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a promising path toward resource-efficient and loss-tolerant quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of quantum repeaters.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and characterizes deep spin defects in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are promising for scalable quantum technologies, but suitable spin defects with long coherence and high readout fidelity were lacking.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization were used to identify deep-level defects in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: A deep-level defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects establish wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and networking.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: Develops a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: Provides a rigorous method to account for device imperfections in security proofs, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: The framework bridges theory and practice, making QKD security proofs more applicable to real-world devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved quantum error correction by turning dominant errors into erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, unifying several symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithms and complexity theory.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but simultaneous optimization is challenging.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol are employed to optimize gate and readout fidelities.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% are achieved for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device.
conclusion: This work advances the practicality of superconducting quantum processors by demonstrating that all key operations can be performed with ultra-high fidelity in a single device.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the behavior of the coherent information under local noise.
result: They identify a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal features near the transition.
conclusion: The work provides a simple mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across scales, challenging conventional methods and providing new insights.

title: Distributed Quantum Dense Coding Enhanced With Nonclassical Routing
authors: Pratham Hullamballi, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Pratham Hullamballi, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We propose a distributed quantum dense coding protocol that uses a control system to superpose two dense coding processes, allowing us to simultaneously and coherently encode and nonclassically route the sender's single-qubit system to two receiver laboratories. We find that dense coding with cohere…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012605] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distributed quantum dense coding protocol with nonclassical routing that superposes two dense coding processes to encode and route a single-qubit system to two receivers.
motivation: To enhance the capacity and flexibility of quantum dense coding by enabling simultaneous encoding and routing to multiple receivers, which is not possible with standard dense coding.
method: The protocol uses a control system to create a superposition of two dense coding processes, allowing the sender's qubit to be coherently encoded and routed to two receiver laboratories via nonclassical routing.
result: The protocol achieves higher information capacity and enables distributed encoding with nonclassical routing, demonstrating advantages over standard dense coding.
conclusion: Distributed quantum dense coding with nonclassical routing offers a new approach for quantum communication networks, potentially improving efficiency and enabling new applications.

title: Engineering Selective Transitions In Dressed Two-qubit Systems With Dual Driving
authors: Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, And Ziyu Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, and Ziyu Tao

Recent experimental progress on dual-rail superconducting qubits has demonstrated millisecond-scale coherence, high-fidelity qubit gates, and multiqubit entanglement, offering a promising path towards resource-efficient quantum error correction. Fast reset and rapid state preparation are becoming cr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to engineer selective transitions in dressed two-qubit systems using dual driving, enabling fast and high-fidelity quantum gates for dual-rail superconducting qubits.
motivation: Dual-rail superconducting qubits show promise for error correction but require fast reset and state preparation. The authors aim to achieve selective transitions without crosstalk to improve gate performance.
method: They propose a dual-driving scheme that dresses the two-qubit system, using carefully designed pulse sequences to selectively excite target transitions while suppressing unwanted ones.
result: The scheme achieves high-fidelity selective transitions with reduced crosstalk, enabling fast reset and state preparation in dual-rail qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical technique for improving gate fidelity and speed in dual-rail superconducting qubit platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Remote Magnon-phonon Entanglement In Waveguide Magnomechanics
authors: Shi-Fan Qi And Fan Li
abstract:
Author(s): Shi-fan Qi and Fan Li

Generating long-distance quantum entanglement is crucial for advancing quantum information processing. In this work, we propose a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a hybrid waveguide magnomechanical system, where multiple spatially separated magnon modes couple to a common…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013702] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a waveguide magnomechanical system.
motivation: Long-distance entanglement is crucial for quantum information processing; this work aims to generate it in a hybrid magnomechanical platform.
method: Uses a waveguide to couple spatially separated magnon modes to a common phonon mode, enabling entanglement via parametric interactions.
result: Demonstrates that remote magnon-phonon entanglement can be achieved with high fidelity under realistic experimental parameters.
conclusion: The protocol offers a viable path for scalable quantum networks using hybrid magnomechanical systems.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperature states.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from spatial-only to spatiotemporal dynamics, enabling new regimes like negative temperatures and wave condensation.
method: The authors derive a thermodynamic description based on wave kinetic equations and a grand-canonical formalism, validated by numerical simulations of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
result: They show that spatiotemporal dynamics lead to equilibrium states with positive or negative temperatures, and identify a condensation transition analogous to Bose-Einstein condensation.
conclusion: The work provides a unified thermodynamic framework for multimode optical systems, with implications for understanding non-equilibrium phenomena and potential applications in photonics.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology exploits quantum phase transitions for enhanced precision, but critical slowing down limits achievable precision within finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental scaling bound using information-theoretic and thermodynamic arguments, relating precision to evolution time and critical exponents.
result: The bound shows that the precision scales as T^{-1/2} for finite-time measurements, independent of critical exponent, revealing a universal trade-off.
conclusion: The scaling limit is fundamental and cannot be circumvented by standard critical metrology protocols, guiding optimal design of quantum sensors.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistical learning method to verify approximate k-designs using randomized measurements, reducing the number of required measurements.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum state ensemble forms an approximate k-design is crucial for many quantum information tasks, but existing methods require many measurements. A more efficient verification protocol is needed.
method: The authors use randomized measurements and a statistical learning approach to estimate the k-th moment of the ensemble, leveraging concentration of measure to reduce sample complexity.
result: They demonstrate that their method can verify approximate k-designs with significantly fewer measurements than previous approaches, and provide theoretical guarantees.
conclusion: The work offers a practical and efficient tool for certifying random state ensembles, which is important for benchmarking quantum devices and studying many-body physics.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and measurements, with applications to quantum error correction and entanglement distribution.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, especially in variational algorithms, error correction, and quantum repeaters.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement (SPAM) setup to iteratively purify noisy qubit states and measurements through a series of swap tests and postselection.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity purified states and measurements with polynomial overhead, and is robust against common noise models.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate SPAM errors, enhancing the performance of near-term quantum devices and quantum network components.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing Rydberg gate pulses for logical error suppression improves surface code performance by mitigating leakage propagation.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions faces leakage errors that degrade surface code performance; existing optimizations focus on physical fidelity rather than logical error rates.
method: The authors model Rydberg leakage mechanisms and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage propagation, then simulate surface code logical error rates under these optimized gates.
result: The optimized gates significantly reduce logical error rates compared to gates optimized for physical fidelity alone, demonstrating improved fault-tolerance thresholds.
conclusion: Gate optimization targeting logical errors is a promising strategy for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage on an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, moving beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, quantifying the computational advantage through entanglement measures and sampling tasks.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, meaning the task is beyond classical simulation capabilities and yields useful output.
conclusion: The work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantage, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers potential for high key rates but faces challenges in security proofs and practical implementation; discrete modulation can improve performance.
method: The authors combine discrete modulation with advanced security analysis tools, including the entropy accumulation theorem, to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, demonstrating the feasibility of high-speed, secure quantum communication.
conclusion: This work brings high-rate, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment, with implications for quantum network scalability.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using radiation sources and measuring error correlations.
result: They observe that ionizing radiation causes spatially and temporally correlated phase errors, which persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts pose a significant obstacle to fault-tolerant quantum computing, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop a theoretical framework linking it to state compression and measurement complexity.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a faithful measure of non-Gaussianity, with operational interpretations in terms of resource requirements for state preparation, compression, and tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, advancing the resource theory of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phases, such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating new phenomena in driven-dissipative systems.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering exotic quantum states in hybrid cavity QED systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Quantum control via counterdiabatic driving is limited by the complexity of exact protocols; variational approaches offer approximations but can be improved.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design variational counterdiabatic driving protocols, optimizing for fidelity.
result: The method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, demonstrated on several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely using superconducting circuit technology and impedance matching techniques.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking through previous performance limits for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in hybrid quantum systems where microwave-to-optical conversion or amplification is required.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to a single cavity via spatial or frequency multiplexing, enabling parallel gate operations.
result: Demonstrates that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed simultaneously without sacrificing cavity enhancement.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing offers a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced operations to large neutral-atom arrays, advancing quantum computing platforms.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from state demolition and long measurement times, limiting qudit performance.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action.
result: The protocol achieves 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout significantly enhances nondemolition measurements, making it a valuable tool for multilevel quantum systems across platforms.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, their security guarantees, and limitations, along with state-of-the-art photonic implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the field is progressing towards more complex protocols.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral
