It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter may be inconsistent; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to constrain possible theories.
method: The authors review theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing the information-theoretic assumptions and experimental feasibility.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, and the review clarifies how entanglement generation would signal the quantum nature of gravity, while absence would constrain modifications.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity, with near-term tabletop experiments being promising.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing. This tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to this approach.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including the role of entanglement and scaling of quantum Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates that critical quantum sensors can surpass the standard quantum limit and approach the Heisenberg limit, with practical considerations for implementation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation sensors, with potential applications in metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but single-shot fluorescence readout at the single-photon level suffers from low signal-to-noise ratio.
method: The authors combine a Bayesian estimator with a neural network trained on experimental data to classify qubit states from weak fluorescence signals, achieving high accuracy with minimal photons.
result: The method achieves readout fidelity above 99% with an average of only 1.5 photons per shot, significantly reducing atom loss and heating.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient, minimally destructive readout for large-scale neutral atom quantum processors, advancing practical quantum computing.

title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems constantly dissipate energy, and extending this paradigm to quantum systems requires a proper description of the environment and dissipation, which is currently lacking.
method: The authors derive a quantum master equation for active particles interacting with a thermal bath, incorporating both coherent driving and dissipative processes, and analyze the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
result: They identify conditions under which quantum active matter exhibits directed motion and show that dissipation can be tuned to control the active behavior, with potential applications in quantum heat engines and information processing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational framework for quantum active matter, highlighting the role of dissipation and offering new insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Doubling Qubits In A Trapped-ion System Via Vibrational Dual-rail Encoding
authors: Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, And Joonsuk Huh
abstract:
Author(s): Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, and Joonsuk Huh

Vibrational modes of trapped ions have traditionally served as quantum buses to mediate entanglement between internal qubits. However, with recent advances in quantum control, it has become possible to use these modes directly as quantum computational resources. Here, we propose a dual-rail encoding…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012408] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a dual-rail encoding scheme using vibrational modes of trapped ions to double the number of qubits without increasing ion count.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum computers are limited by the number of ions that can be stably trapped; using vibrational modes as qubits can increase computational resources without adding more ions.
method: The authors design a dual-rail encoding where each ion's vibrational mode represents a logical qubit, and show how to implement single- and two-qubit gates using existing control techniques.
result: The scheme effectively doubles the number of qubits available in a trapped-ion system with current technology, and gate fidelities are estimated to be high enough for practical quantum computation.
conclusion: Vibrational dual-rail encoding is a viable near-term approach to scale trapped-ion quantum computers without requiring additional ions or major hardware changes.

title: Unbounded Sequence Of Observers Exhibiting Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Steering Via Probabilistic Projective Measurements
authors: Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, And Hui-Juan Zuo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, and Hui-Juan Zuo

Recent studies have demonstrated that coherent weak measurements allow Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering to be shared sequentially between a single Alice and multiple Bobs. Theoretically, this permits an unbounded sequence in the high-dimensional limit. In this work, we investigate whether the experi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012411] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that an unbounded sequence of observers can exhibit Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering using probabilistic projective measurements, extending previous weak measurement results.
motivation: Previous work demonstrated sequential EPR steering sharing with weak measurements, but it was unclear if projective measurements could achieve an unbounded sequence. This paper aims to prove that probabilistic projective measurements can also enable an unbounded number of observers.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a scenario where Alice performs a projective measurement on one half of a maximally entangled pair, and multiple Bobs sequentially perform probabilistic projective measurements on the other half. They derive conditions for steering sharing and show that in the high-dimensional limit, the number of Bobs can be unbounded.
result: They prove that with probabilistic projective measurements, an unbounded sequence of Bobs can demonstrate EPR steering, and they provide explicit measurement strategies that achieve this.
conclusion: Probabilistic projective measurements are sufficient for unbounded sequential EPR steering sharing, which has implications for quantum communication and foundational tests of quantum mechanics.

title: Emergence Of non-Markovian Decoherent Histories In An Integrable Environment: A Tape-recorder Model For Local Quantum Observables
authors: Nataliya Arefyeva And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Nataliya Arefyeva and Evgeny Polyakov

We propose an alternative approach to the coarse-grained description of quantum evolution that provides an explicit recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories in a controlled way, applicable to non-Markovian and integrable systems. Specifically, we study the local interaction qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062225] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained decoherent histories approach for non-Markovian integrable systems, using a tape-recorder model to describe local quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding decoherence and the emergence of classicality in quantum systems, especially non-Markovian and integrable environments, is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors develop a controlled recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories, applying it to a local interaction quench in an integrable environment modeled as a tape recorder.
result: They demonstrate that non-Markovian effects can be captured within the decoherent histories framework, and the tape-recorder model yields well-defined histories for local observables.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to study decoherence and classicality in complex quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Stochastic resetting with conditional measurements leads to nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics.
motivation: To understand how stochastic resetting and global measurements can generate nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior in noninteracting systems.
method: The authors study a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting, where the reset state depends on the outcome of a global measurement. They analyze the dynamics and steady-state properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, indicating a phase transition driven by the measurement and resetting protocol.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting with conditional measurements can induce complex nonequilibrium phenomena even in noninteracting systems, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of conserved quantities after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding the statistics of fluctuations in large regions after quantum quenches is a fundamental challenge in non-equilibrium many-body physics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of conserved charges in integrable systems, treating the quench as a source of ballistic transport and incorporating initial state correlations.
result: They derive exact formulas for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations follow a large deviation principle with a rate function given by the thermodynamic entropy production.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for fluctuation statistics in quantum quenches, bridging non-equilibrium dynamics and thermodynamics, and provides testable predictions for experiments.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of different state preparation protocols for topological states, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Numerical study of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: The engineered dissipation protocol achieves faster preparation times and higher fidelities compared to passive cooling.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state engineering.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: To realize and study synchronization in the quantum regime, which is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics with potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to create two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, with the synchronized state encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible through joint measurement.
result: Successful observation of synchronization between the two quantum oscillators, evidenced by a fixed relative phase.
conclusion: The work demonstrates quantum synchronization in a controlled experimental platform, opening avenues for studying collective quantum phenomena and their applications.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors combine experimental results with numerical analysis to study the dynamics of a nonlinear coupling designed to suppress these transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, enabling higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical improvement for transmon readout, contributing to better qubit performance in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation without exhaustive sampling.
result: The framework successfully identifies the number and properties of spin bath constituents in simulated and experimental NV center data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient, scalable tool for quantum model learning and parameter estimation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and minimal disturbance remains challenging. Existing methods often cause atom loss or heating.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atom arrays. They use a probe-pump scheme in a finite magnetic field to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio and reduce scattering.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging with low atom loss and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, enabling scalable quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical path for scalable neutral-atom quantum computing, combining high fidelity with low perturbation.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. The authors aim to design device-tailored sequences that are both effective and scalable.
method: The paper maps the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting principles to cancel k-local noise. The resulting sequences are derived from code properties.
result: The proposed sequences achieve decoupling from spatially correlated noise with a length that does not scale with the number of qubits, offering a practical advantage for multi-qubit systems.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a systematic way to generate efficient, tailored decoupling sequences for realistic noise models.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer tailored optical interactions in a fully optical system to create an effective negative-mass oscillator that coherently cancels quantum backaction.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing confinement in quantum simulators and may reveal new non-equilibrium phenomena.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to study string-breaking dynamics in a quantum spin chain, considering both adiabatic and diabatic regimes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics beyond simple decay, including oscillatory and multi-string behavior.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics of confined systems and suggests experimental probes for quantum simulators.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable quantum communication, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (finite-size, composable), and experimental implementations, as well as CV quantum networks and other CV communication tasks.
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with commercial systems, record-breaking key rates, and ongoing advances in security proofs and network demonstrations.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive approach for practical quantum networks, with continued progress expected in security, distance, and integration with classical infrastructure.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is challenging. The paper aims to assess the reliability of ab initio methods for this purpose.
method: The authors review cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for modeling spin-spin relaxation in various solid-state spin qubits, discussing their successes and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of spin qubits with long coherence times, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Heisenberg-Scaling Characterization Of A Two-Channel Optical Network Via Two-Port Homodyne Detection
authors: Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, And Vincenzo Tamma
abstract:
Author(s): Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, and Vincenzo Tamma

We present a fully Gaussian and experimentally feasible scheme for the simultaneous estimation of the four real parameters that characterize a two-channel optical network. The scheme utilizes a two-mode squeezed probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports, for which we derive the comp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010801] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A Gaussian scheme for simultaneous estimation of four parameters of a two-channel optical network using two-mode squeezed light and homodyne detection achieves Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Characterizing optical networks with high precision is crucial for quantum information processing; simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters can improve efficiency.
method: The scheme uses a two-mode squeezed vacuum probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports; the Fisher information matrix is derived to analyze estimation precision.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling for all four parameters, with the quantum Fisher information matrix being diagonal and proportional to the total photon number squared.
conclusion: The proposed fully Gaussian and experimentally feasible scheme enables Heisenberg-limited multiparameter estimation in optical networks, with potential applications in quantum metrology and network characterization.

title: Microscopic Rydberg Electron Orbit Manipulation With Optical Tweezers
authors: Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, And Florian Meinert
abstract:
Author(s): Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, and Florian Meinert

Laser cooling and trapping of atomic matter waves in optical potentials has enabled rapid progress in quantum science, particularly when combined with Rydberg excitation of the atoms to induce long-range interactions. Here, we propose the local manipulation and spatiotemporal sculpting of the electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes local manipulation of Rydberg electron orbitals using optical tweezers to create tailored long-range interactions.
motivation: To enable spatiotemporal sculpting of Rydberg electron wavefunctions for advanced quantum simulation and information processing.
method: Theoretical proposal combining optical tweezers with Rydberg excitation to locally control electron orbitals.
result: Demonstrates that optical tweezers can manipulate Rydberg electron orbitals, enabling tunable anisotropic interactions.
conclusion: This technique offers a new tool for engineering interactions in quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and networking.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: Understanding necessary conditions for directed currents in nonequilibrium systems is fundamental; the ratchet principle is widely used but may be incomplete.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying hidden conservation laws that suppress currents.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents despite symmetry breaking, providing a counterexample to the naive ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be refined to account for hidden conservation laws, which are crucial for predicting directed transport in stochastic systems.

title: Genuinely Nonlocal Sets With Smallest Cardinality
authors: Zong-Xing Xiong, Mao-Sheng Li, Bing Yu, Zhu-Jun Zheng, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zong-Xing Xiong, Mao-Sheng Li, Bing Yu, Zhu-Jun Zheng, and Lvzhou Li

Recently, there has been growing interest in the study of genuine nonlocality, which serves to explore the local accessibility of global information encoded in orthogonal multipartite quantum states under scenarios where not all subsystems are joined together. For this form of nonlocality, a probabl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012410] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies the smallest cardinality of genuinely nonlocal sets of orthogonal multipartite quantum states, proving that for any number of parties, a set of size 2 can be genuinely nonlocal.
motivation: Genuine nonlocality captures the local accessibility of global information in multipartite states when not all subsystems can be joined. Determining the minimal size of such sets is a fundamental question.
method: The authors construct explicit examples of genuinely nonlocal sets with only two orthogonal states for any number of parties, using a combination of local projective measurements and analysis of orthogonality-preserving local operations.
result: They prove that for any number of parties, there exist genuinely nonlocal sets of size 2, which is the smallest possible cardinality. This improves previous lower bounds and resolves an open problem.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the minimal cardinality of genuinely nonlocal sets, advancing the understanding of multipartite nonlocality and local accessibility of quantum information.

title: Quantum Resource Theory Of $π$-ordered Coherence
authors: Xiaofei Qi, Bing Xu, Zhijie Wang, And Jinchuan Hou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofei Qi, Bing Xu, Zhijie Wang, and Jinchuan Hou

Within the framework of resource theory, the research on quantum coherence has not only furnished a rigorous and systematic methodology for investigating quantum coherence and developing coherence quantification methods, but also tackled key issues regarding the conversion and practical utilization …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012417] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for π-ordered coherence, a specific type of quantum coherence, and provides a complete characterization of its free operations and monotones.
motivation: Quantum coherence is a key resource in quantum information, but different types of coherence (e.g., π-ordered coherence) require tailored resource theories to understand their manipulation and quantification.
method: The authors define π-ordered coherence via a partial order on the energy eigenbasis and characterize the set of free operations (π-incoherent operations) and free states. They then construct a family of coherence monotones based on the π-order.
result: They prove that the π-ordered coherence is a valid resource theory with a complete set of monotones, and they show that the relative entropy of π-ordered coherence is a faithful measure. They also provide conditions for state conversion under π-incoherent operations.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous resource-theoretic framework for π-ordered coherence, which may find applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing where coherence in a specific order matters.

title: Collective Vibronic Cascade In Cavity-coupled Jahn-Teller Active Molecules
authors: Suraj Kumar Pandit, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar, And Krishna R. Nandipati
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Kumar Pandit, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar, and Krishna R. Nandipati

We study the polaritonic states and dynamics of multiple Jahn-Teller (JT) active molecules coupled to the modes of a Fabry-Perot cavity. We find that collective effects dramatically alter the interplay of electronic, vibrational, and cavity angular momenta, giving rise to markedly different polarito…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012802] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective vibronic effects in Jahn-Teller active molecules coupled to a Fabry-Perot cavity, revealing new polaritonic states and dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how collective effects in cavity-coupled molecular systems alter electronic, vibrational, and cavity angular momenta is important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the polaritonic states and dynamics of multiple Jahn-Teller active molecules coupled to cavity modes, using a model that includes electronic, vibrational, and cavity degrees of freedom.
result: Collective effects lead to markedly different polaritonic states compared to single-molecule coupling, with altered interplay of angular momenta.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the design of hybrid quantum systems involving molecular ensembles and optical cavities.

title: Three-dimensional Squeezing Of Optically Levitated Nanospheres
authors: Giacomo Marocco, David C. Moore, And Daniel Carney
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Marocco, David C. Moore, and Daniel Carney

We propose a protocol to measure three-dimensional impulses beyond the standard quantum limit. The protocol reduces noise in all three spatial dimensions and consists of squeezing a mechanical system's state via a series of jumps in the frequency of the harmonic potential. We quantify how decoherenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for three-dimensional squeezing of optically levitated nanospheres to measure impulses beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Optically levitated nanospheres are promising for force sensing but limited by quantum noise; squeezing can enhance sensitivity.
method: The protocol uses a series of jumps in the harmonic potential frequency to squeeze the mechanical state in all three spatial dimensions, and analyzes decoherence effects.
result: The protocol reduces noise in all three dimensions, enabling measurement of three-dimensional impulses beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible method for quantum-enhanced force sensing with levitated nanoparticles, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Subradiant Collective States For Precision Sensing Via Transmission Spectra
authors: Diego Zafra-Bono, Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, And Susanne F. Yelin
abstract:
Author(s): Diego Zafra-Bono, Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, and Susanne F. Yelin

The authors propose a quantum metrology framework that harnesses the narrow linewidths of subradiant collective states in subwavelength emitter arrays. By introducing spatially varying control detunings to couple dark and bright modes, they show that the resulting sharp features in the transmission spectrum enable the precise detection of both global and local perturbations under realistic experimental imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013704] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using subradiant collective states in subwavelength emitter arrays for precision sensing via transmission spectra.
motivation: Subradiant states have narrow linewidths that are sensitive to perturbations, but they are dark and hard to probe. The authors aim to harness these states for metrology by coupling them to bright modes.
method: They introduce spatially varying control detunings to couple dark subradiant modes to bright superradiant modes, creating sharp features in the transmission spectrum that can be used for sensing.
result: The proposed scheme enables precise detection of both global and local perturbations, and is robust to realistic experimental imperfections such as position disorder and finite array size.
conclusion: Subradiant collective states in emitter arrays offer a promising platform for quantum sensing, leveraging narrow linewidths for high precision.

title: Nonreciprocal Phonon Blockade In Spin Quadratic Optomechanical Systems
authors: Yao Dong And Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Dong and Guo-Feng Zhang

We propose a scheme for achieving nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system consisting of two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator. Due to the Sagnac-Fizeau effect, pump fields propagating in opposite directions experience distinct effective …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013701] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system with two spinning resonators.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal phonon blockade, which is important for quantum information processing and chiral quantum networks.
method: Uses two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator, exploiting the Sagnac-Fizeau effect to create direction-dependent effective couplings.
result: Demonstrates that nonreciprocal phonon blockade can be realized, with the blockade effect depending on the direction of the pump field.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a platform for nonreciprocal quantum devices and may have applications in quantum information processing.

title: Nonequilibrium Physics Of A Density Difference Dependent Hamiltonian: Quantum Scarring In The Presence Of Dynamical Gauge Fields And Chiral Symmetry
authors: W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, and Tomoki Ozawa

Quantum many-body scars represent a form of weak ergodicity breaking that highlights the unusual physics of thermalization in quantum systems. Understanding scar formation promises insight into the connection between classical statistical mechanics and the quantum world. The existence of quantum man…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars in a model with density-dependent hopping, dynamical gauge fields, and chiral symmetry, revealing non-thermal eigenstates and their stability.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide a window into weak ergodicity breaking and the connection between classical statistical mechanics and quantum thermalization.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional model with density-dependent hopping, which introduces a dynamical gauge field and chiral symmetry, using exact diagonalization and analytical arguments to identify scar states.
result: They find exact scar states with equally spaced energies and non-thermal entanglement entropy, and show that these scars are robust to perturbations that preserve chiral symmetry.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for quantum scarring via density-dependent hopping and gauge fields, expanding the understanding of non-ergodic behavior in many-body systems.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin qubit states using Pauli spin blockade.
motivation: Scalable readout of spin qubits is crucial for quantum computing; existing PSB readout cannot distinguish all four two-qubit states.
method: The authors model a double quantum dot with two spin qubits coupled to a resonator, and analyze the reflected signal phase and amplitude for each two-qubit state under PSB conditions.
result: They show that the four two-qubit states produce distinct reflected signal signatures, enabling full state discrimination via reflectometry.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry can provide a simple, scalable readout scheme for spin qubits without requiring additional sensors.

title: Violation Of The Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem During Domain Growth In The Long-range Ising Model
authors: Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, And Varsha Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, and Varsha Banerjee

The celebrated fluctuation dissipation theorem (FDT) does not apply to nonequilibrium systems. In this context, Cugliandolo and Kurchan [
tldr: This paper studies the violation of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem during domain growth in the long-range Ising model, providing a generalized FDT framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem fails in nonequilibrium systems, and understanding its generalization is crucial for characterizing aging and coarsening dynamics.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of the long-range Ising model with power-law interactions and analyze the two-time correlation and response functions to extract the fluctuation-dissipation ratio.
result: They find that the fluctuation-dissipation ratio exhibits a nontrivial dependence on the interaction range and time scales, revealing distinct aging regimes.
conclusion: The generalized FDT provides a consistent description of nonequilibrium dynamics in long-range interacting systems, with implications for understanding glassy behavior and coarsening.

title: Nonequilibrium (thermo)dynamics Of Colloids Under Mobile Piston Compression
authors: Arturo Moncho-Jordá, José López-Molina, And Joachim Dzubiella
abstract:
Author(s): Arturo Moncho-Jordá, José López-Molina, and Joachim Dzubiella

We investigate the nonequilibrium compression of a confined colloidal fluid driven by a mobile boundary within dynamical density functional theory. The system consists of a hard-sphere fluid confined between two parallel walls, one of which acts as an overdamped piston subjected to a sudden increase…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015403] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium compression of a confined colloidal fluid driven by a mobile piston using dynamical density functional theory.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamics and dynamics of soft matter under nonequilibrium conditions is important for both fundamental physics and applications like microfluidics.
method: The authors employ dynamical density functional theory (DDFT) to model a hard-sphere fluid confined between two walls, with one wall acting as an overdamped piston subjected to a sudden increase in external force.
result: They find that the piston motion and fluid density profiles exhibit complex relaxation dynamics, with the system's free energy and pressure showing hysteresis and memory effects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium thermodynamics of colloidal systems under mechanical compression, relevant to information thermodynamics through the lens of work and dissipation.

title: Score-based Modeling Of Effective Langevin Dynamics
authors: Ludovico Theo Giorgini
abstract:
Author(s): Ludovico Theo Giorgini

We introduce a constructive framework to learn effective Langevin equations from stationary time series. Unlike conventional approaches that require iterative calibration to match target statistics, our construction guarantees the observed steady-state density by design and enforces short-lag coordi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A framework to learn effective Langevin equations from stationary time series that guarantees the observed steady-state density by design.
motivation: Conventional approaches require iterative calibration to match target statistics; this work aims to provide a more direct and principled method.
method: The authors construct a score-based model that enforces the observed steady-state density and short-lag correlations, learning the drift and diffusion terms of the Langevin equation.
result: The method yields effective Langevin equations that accurately reproduce the steady-state distribution and dynamical correlations of the original time series.
conclusion: This framework offers a constructive and efficient way to model effective stochastic dynamics from data, with potential applications in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, through active fluctuations.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter is unclear.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and compare passive (thermal) noise with active (colored) noise, using theoretical models and simulations.
result: They find that active fluctuations can break detailed balance and produce currents even when all symmetries are preserved, challenging the traditional ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be extended to account for non-thermal fluctuations, which has implications for active matter and biological systems.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a BEC and exploiting atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and communication; generating it via a hybrid BEC-optical interface offers a new approach.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective spin excitation in a BEC; during storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution that squeezes the retrieved light.
result: The scheme predicts significant squeezing levels achievable with realistic experimental parameters.
conclusion: This hybrid quantum system combining BEC and optics provides a viable method for on-demand squeezed light generation.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and demonstrates how tensor-network representations enable efficient simulation of non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging. The process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and show how tensor-network techniques (e.g., matrix product operators) can represent process tensors compactly, enabling efficient numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate the approach on several examples, including spin-boson models and impurity problems, showing accurate and efficient simulation of non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The process tensor combined with tensor networks offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating complex non-Markovian quantum systems, with broad applicability in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, demonstrating insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable and robust approach using entangled states.
method: The authors introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise. They analyze the sensing protocol theoretically and demonstrate its robustness.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being immune to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging the noise immunity of Lieb-Mattis states, advancing hybrid quantum systems for sensing applications.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to synthesize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully realize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating high-fidelity control over the quantum harmonic oscillator.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex quantum states, with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent manipulation.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, enabling nondestructive measurement and control.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, with potential applications in information thermodynamics.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, characterizing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage.
motivation: Transmon qubits can escape their computational states into highly excited states (ionization), which degrades performance; understanding this process is crucial for improving readout and coherence.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements on a transmon qubit to map out excited-state transitions and identify multiphoton Landau-Zener dynamics.
result: They observe distinct ionization thresholds and transition rates, revealing the mechanism by which transmons ionize under strong drives.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to design better readout schemes and mitigate leakage errors in superconducting qubits.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks inherently preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting without explicit regularization.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, requiring explicit mechanisms to retain plasticity. Quantum neural networks may offer intrinsic advantages due to their parameter structure.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally verify the plasticity of quantum neural networks under sequential task learning, comparing with classical counterparts.
result: Quantum neural networks maintain high plasticity and avoid catastrophic forgetting as the number of parameters grows, unlike classical networks.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are naturally suited for continual learning, suggesting potential advantages in adaptive quantum machine learning systems.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a broad class of quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) and implement them in a photonic circuit.
result: The simulator can efficiently emulate various quantum field phenomena with high configurability and fidelity.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical photonic approach to quantum simulation, bridging quantum optics and quantum field theory.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them to perform displacement sensing, optimizing the measurement protocol.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing performance, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the strong interactions between Rydberg atoms.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to approximate the desired nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing and quantum simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot measurements of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling detection of noise in the intermediate-frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in a semiconductor qubit platform, revealing previously inaccessible noise features.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, aiding in the development of more coherent quantum devices.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. This work explores collective effects in ensembles to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, deriving the conditions for photon blockade and analyzing the dependence on system size and coupling strengths.
result: They find that collective two-photon interactions lead to enhanced photon blockade with increasing ensemble size, achieving high transmission and strong antibunching even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective effects in emitter ensembles provide a viable route to realize photon blockade for quantum photonic applications without demanding strong single-emitter nonlinearities.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates; current architectures have high space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware and extends it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture makes neutral-atom quantum simulators more practical for large-scale quantum simulation by reducing resource requirements.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure.
result: The method accurately predicts Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth beyond the training time window, demonstrating generalization.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, analyzing how noise affects the variance of gradients and connecting it to the expressivity of the circuit ansatz.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to non-vanishing gradients under certain conditions. Quantitative estimates for the loss function concentration are provided.
conclusion: The work provides a principled link between noise and expressivity, offering a roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms and optimizing training in near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, quantum signal processing, and variable-time amplitude amplification.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, discusses complexity bounds, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and noise.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
