A number of intriguing phenomena, including exciton condensation, orbital ordering, and emergence of chirality, have been proposed to accompany charge-density-wave (CDW) formation in the layered transition metal dichalcogenide [MATH]. Explaining these effects relies on knowl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256101] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice of 1T-TiSe2, focusing on its structural and electronic properties.
motivation: To resolve controversies about the nature of the CDW phase in 1T-TiSe2, including proposals of exciton condensation, orbital ordering, and chirality.
method: The authors use advanced electron microscopy and diffraction techniques to determine the precise atomic structure of the CDW superlattice.
result: They provide a detailed structural model of the CDW phase, clarifying the atomic displacements and ordering.
conclusion: The findings help explain the origin of the CDW and its associated phenomena, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of magnon frequency combs induced by a geometric bump in a magnetic film.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnonic systems for potential applications in signal processing.
method: Microwave pumping of a yttrium iron garnet film with a lithographically defined bump, combined with Brillouin light scattering microscopy to detect spin-wave spectra.
result: A magnon frequency comb with equally spaced peaks is observed, arising from three-magnon scattering processes enhanced by the curvature.
conclusion: Curvature-induced magnon frequency combs provide a new platform for studying nonlinear magnonics and may enable compact frequency comb generators.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskites via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter physics, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical calculations were used to study carrier-strain-mediated spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: A giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate a new mechanism for controlling spin and carrier dynamics in chiral perovskites, with potential applications in optoelectronics.

title: Curvature Instability Of An Active Gel Growing On A Wavy Membrane
authors: Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, And Pierre Sens

Cell shape changes are largely controlled by the actin cytoskeleton, a dynamic filament network beneath the plasma membrane. Several cell types can form extended freestanding protrusions not supported by an extracellular substrate or matrix, and regulated by proteins sensitive to the cell membrane c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 258401] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the curvature instability of an active gel growing on a wavy membrane, relevant to cell shape changes and actin cytoskeleton dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how cells form extended protrusions not supported by extracellular matrix is important for cell biology, but the paper focuses on biophysical modeling of active gels and membranes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of an active gel layer growing on a deformable membrane with wavy geometry, analyzing the conditions for curvature instability.
result: They find that active stresses can drive instability leading to membrane protrusions, with growth rate depending on wavenumber and active parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into cytoskeleton-driven cell shape changes, but it is primarily a biophysics paper without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Efficient Privacy-preserving Training Of Quantum Neural Networks Through Ensemble Encoding Of Quantum States
authors: Gaoyuan Wang, Jonathan Warrell, And Mark Gerstein
abstract:
Author(s): Gaoyuan Wang, Jonathan Warrell, and Mark Gerstein

Quantum computing is gaining popularity due to its potential to detect complex patterns in data by leveraging unique quantum phenomena. It is particularly promising for complex data applications, such as those in biomedicine. However, in these contexts, it is often necessary to share and then aggreg…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012413] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving training method for quantum neural networks using ensemble encoding of quantum states.
motivation: Quantum machine learning on sensitive data (e.g., biomedical) requires privacy guarantees, but existing methods are inefficient or insecure.
method: The authors introduce an ensemble encoding scheme where multiple copies of a quantum state are used to represent data, combined with differential privacy noise to protect individual data points during training.
result: The method achieves privacy guarantees with lower overhead compared to standard differential privacy approaches, while maintaining model accuracy on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: Ensemble encoding offers a practical trade-off between privacy and utility for quantum neural network training, but the work is primarily a machine learning application with limited quantum information theory contribution.

title: Improved Delta-kick Cooling With Multiple Nonideal Kicks
authors: Harshil Neeraj, David C. Spierings, Joseph Mcgowan IV, Nicholas Mantella, And Aephraim M. Steinberg
abstract:
Author(s): Harshil Neeraj, David C. Spierings, Joseph McGowan IV, Nicholas Mantella, and Aephraim M. Steinberg

Delta-kick cooling is a technique employed to achieve low kinetic temperatures by decreasing momentum width at the cost of increased position width. In an ideal implementation, this method uses a harmonic potential to deliver a single near-instantaneous momentum kick. In practice, potentials that ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013101] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves delta-kick cooling for ultracold atoms by analyzing multiple nonideal kicks, but it is an atomic physics technique unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Delta-kick cooling is used to achieve low kinetic temperatures in ultracold atom experiments, but practical potentials are nonideal. The authors aim to improve cooling by using multiple kicks.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally study delta-kick cooling with multiple nonideal kicks, modeling the effect of anharmonic potentials and optimizing kick sequences.
result: They show that multiple kicks can compensate for nonidealities and achieve lower temperatures than a single kick, with detailed analysis of momentum and position distributions.
conclusion: Multiple nonideal kicks can improve delta-kick cooling performance, providing a practical method for colder atomic samples.

title: Probing Short-range Gravity Using Quantum Reflection
authors: J. Boynewicz And C. A. Sackett
abstract:

Quantum reflection occurs when ultracold atoms are incident on a material surface with sufficiently low velocity. The reflecting matter wave can interfere with the incident wave to form a detectable pattern, and this pattern contains information about atom-surface interactions at micrometer scales. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum reflection of ultracold atoms to probe short-range gravity, which is a quantum sensing application not aligned with the user's research directions.
motivation: To test gravity at micrometer scales using quantum interference effects.
method: Ultracold atoms are reflected from a material surface; the interference pattern between incident and reflected matter waves is analyzed to extract atom-surface interaction information.
result: The interference pattern provides constraints on short-range gravitational forces.
conclusion: Quantum reflection can be a sensitive probe for short-range gravity, but the work is primarily a metrology application.

We study the ground-state and low-lying metastable phases of repulsive binary Bose-Einstein condensates confined in twisted, spin-dependent periodic optical lattices. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 013302] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies emergent quasiperiodic order in Bose-Bose mixtures with spin-dependent periodic potentials.
motivation: To understand the ground-state and metastable phases of binary Bose-Einstein condensates in twisted optical lattices.
method: Theoretical analysis of repulsive binary BECs in spin-dependent periodic optical lattices, examining momentum-space symmetry and phase transitions.
result: Weak intercomponent interactions lead to fourfold momentum-space symmetry; quasiperiodic order emerges from the interplay of lattice geometry and interactions.
conclusion: The work reveals novel ordering phenomena in multicomponent BECs but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effective Theory Of Surface Oscillations In Self-bound Superfluid Droplets
authors: Jun Mitsuhashi, Keisuke Fujii, And Masaru Hongo

We investigate the low-energy dynamics of small-amplitude surface oscillations of spherical superfluid droplets in vacuum. Starting from the effective field theory of superfluid phonons, we derive an effective action governing the surface oscillations under a fixed particle-number constraint. The no…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an effective field theory for surface oscillations of superfluid droplets, focusing on low-energy dynamics under fixed particle number.
motivation: To understand the low-energy dynamics of surface oscillations in self-bound superfluid droplets, which are relevant for atomic and molecular physics.
method: Starting from an effective field theory of superfluid phonons, the authors derive an effective action for surface oscillations with a fixed particle-number constraint.
result: They obtain a description of surface oscillations that includes the effects of the particle-number constraint and derive the dispersion relation.
conclusion: The effective theory provides a framework for studying surface modes in superfluid droplets, with potential applications to finite-size quantum systems.

title: Vortex Dynamics In Rotating Dipolar Supersolids Across Josephson And Self-trapping Regimes
authors: Aitor Alaña, Michele Modugno, And Pablo Capuzzi

We investigate vortex nucleation and transport in a rotating dipolar supersolid arranged in a triangular droplet lattice, exploiting its description as an array of weakly linked condensates. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 013305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies vortex dynamics in rotating dipolar supersolids, focusing on Josephson and self-trapping regimes in a triangular droplet lattice.
motivation: Understanding vortex nucleation and transport in supersolids is important for characterizing these exotic quantum phases.
method: The authors model the supersolid as an array of weakly linked condensates and analyze phase differences to study vortex dynamics.
result: They show that local phase differences lead to distinct Josephson and self-trapping dynamics for vortices.
conclusion: The work provides insights into vortex behavior in supersolids but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optical Coprocessor Based On Spontaneous Brillouin Scattering
authors: I. V. Vovchenko, A. A. Zyablovsky, A. A. Pukhov, And E. S. Andrianov
abstract:
Author(s): I. V. Vovchenko, A. A. Zyablovsky, A. A. Pukhov, and E. S. Andrianov

Analog coprocessors for neural networks are an intensively developing field. They provide approximate results of computations for relatively low energy cost and at high speed. We show that a set of ring resonators with Brillouin interaction between photons and phonons, being coupled to a waveguide, …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013501] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an optical coprocessor using Brillouin scattering in ring resonators for analog neural network computation.
motivation: Analog coprocessors offer approximate computation with low energy cost and high speed, which is attractive for neural networks.
method: The authors model a set of ring resonators with Brillouin interaction between photons and phonons, coupled to a waveguide, to perform matrix-vector multiplications.
result: The system can implement linear operations for neural network inference, with potential for high speed and low power consumption.
conclusion: The proposed Brillouin-based optical coprocessor is a promising approach for analog computing, though it is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Temporal Parity-time Phase Transition In Photonic Time-modulated Media

tldr: This paper studies temporal parity-time phase transitions in photonic time-modulated media, focusing on non-Hermitian wave dynamics and effective gain/loss.
motivation: To understand how temporal modulation of photonic media can induce non-Hermitian dynamics and phase transitions, which is a topic in classical wave physics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a temporally PT-symmetric modulation scheme and prove conditions for Hermiticity and phase transitions.

conclusion: The work provides insights into non-Hermitian photonics but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

In this paper we numerically and statistically investigate the integrable turbulence of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger sys…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063535] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically and statistically studies integrable turbulence in a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing, focusing on rogue-wave generation.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems through integrable turbulence.
method: Numerical simulations and statistical analysis of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing effect.
result: The study reveals statistical properties and dynamical behaviors of integrable turbulence, including rogue-wave statistics.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of integrable turbulence and rogue-wave formation in nonlinear wave systems.

title: Generalized Stokes Formalism For Partially Coherent Higher-order Vector Vortex Beams

A mathematical formalism of the generalized Stokes field is developed to characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams (PC-HOVVBs) in two configurations: (1) without double-slit and (2) with double-slit. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063536] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized Stokes formalism for partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, focusing on propagation through double-slit configurations.
motivation: To characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, which are important for classical and quantum optics applications.
method: The authors extend the Stokes field formalism to include higher-order vector vortex beams and analyze propagation with and without a double-slit using mathematical modeling.
result: The generalized Stokes field formalism successfully describes the propagation behavior and coherence properties of these beams in both configurations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fractional Skyrmions By Fractional Orbital Angular Momentum
authors: Yuancong Cao, Ram Nandan Kumar, Hadrian Bezuidenhout, Mingjian Cheng, Lixin Guo, And Andrew Forbes

motivation: Optical Skyrmions with integer topological numbers are robust to complex media; extending to fractional Skyrmions could enable new applications in optical manipulation and information encoding.
method: The authors structure light as a vectorial superposition of fractional orbital angular momentum modes to generate optical Skyrmions with noninteger Skyrmion numbers.
result: Fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers are experimentally demonstrated.
conclusion: Fractional Skyrmions expand the family of optical topologies and may offer additional degrees of freedom for optical communication and manipulation.

title: Interacting Many-body non-Hermitian Systems As Markov Chains
authors: Zichang Hao, Wei Jie Chan, And Ching Hua Lee
abstract:

Rich phenomenology emerges at the intersection of non-Hermiticity and many-body dynamics, yet physically realizable implementations remain challenging. In this work, we propose a general formalism that maps non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians to the Laplacians of Markov chains, such that wave-funct…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014301] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Maps non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians to Markov chain Laplacians, revealing non-equilibrium steady states and topological properties.
motivation: Non-Hermitian many-body systems are difficult to realize physically; a mapping to Markov chains could simplify analysis and connect to stochastic processes.
method: The authors propose a general formalism that maps non-Hermitian Hamiltonians to Laplacians of Markov chains, using the wave-function as a probability distribution.
result: The mapping reveals non-equilibrium steady states and topological features such as spectral winding and skin effects in many-body systems.
conclusion: This formalism provides a new perspective on non-Hermitian many-body physics, linking it to classical stochastic processes and potentially enabling experimental realizations.

A wide variety of experimental platforms, ranging from semiconductor quantum-dot arrays to moiré materials, have recently emerged as powerful quantum simulators for studying the Hubbard model and its variants. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 014402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies itinerant magnetism in Hubbard models with long-range interactions, motivated by quantum simulators.
motivation: To understand magnetic phases in generalized Hubbard models relevant to experimental platforms like quantum-dot arrays and moiré materials.
method: The authors investigate a Hubbard model with long-range interactions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They characterize the magnetic phase diagram and identify regimes of itinerant magnetism.

result: Observation of complex magnetic and transport phenomena due to dual magnetic sublattices.
conclusion: The material exhibits interesting magnetic and transport properties, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies coupled spin-charge states in a decorated honeycomb lattice using hybrid Monte Carlo, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dc Spin Current Driven By Low-frequency Light In Altermagnets

result: They find that small in-plane magnetic fields can induce transitions from incommensurate to commensurate phases.
conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into magnetic phase transitions but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Role Of Interstitial Anionic Electrons In High-pressure Li-Pd Superconducting Electrides

title: Rashba-driven Insights Into Molecular Excitons
authors: Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, And Vladimir Chernyak
abstract:

Emmanuel Rashba’s enduring influence on molecular exciton physics is reflected in several foundational concepts: excitons in the narrow-band limit, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, the giant oscillator strength of shallow impurity-bound excitons, and isotopic editing as a quantitative spectroscopic tool. method: The paper is a review that synthesizes Rashba's key concepts and their impact on modern multiscale modeling and excitonic functionality.
result: Rashba's insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors and molecular aggregates.
conclusion: Rashba's vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in quantum and optoelectronic materials.

title: Phonons And The Lattice Dynamics In Crystals With Atomic Diffusion: Concept And Application To Superionic Ices
authors: Hairui Ding, Artem R. Oganov, Haixu Cui, Jiachang Zhang, And Xiao Dong

conclusion: The work provides a new tool for studying vibrational properties in partially disordered crystals, with implications for understanding superionic conductors.

title: Non-self-averaging Topological Anderson Insulator
authors: Zheng-Wei Zuo And Jun-Chong Liu

Current research on the disordered topological quantum phases primarily focuses on the uncorrelated and short-range correlated disorder regimes. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 024201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.

title: Non-Hermitian Comb Effect In Coupled Clean And Quasiperiodic Chains

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024202] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain, focusing on the non-Hermitian comb effect.
motivation: Understanding localization in non-Hermitian systems with quasiperiodic potentials is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a system of two coupled chains, one clean and one quasiperiodic, with non-Hermitian terms, using numerical methods to study localization properties.
result: They find transitions from delocalized to intermediate phases as non-Hermiticity increases, and identify a non-Hermitian comb effect.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of localization in non-Hermitian systems but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Impact Of Stealthy Hyperuniform Magnetic Impurity Configurations On Bulk Magnetism In A Two-dimensional Heisenberg Model
authors: Kota Asakura, Kazuki Yamamoto, And Akihisa Koga
abstract:

We investigate an antiferromagnetic quantum Heisenberg model on a square lattice with high-spin magnetic impurities to clarify how random and stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations influence the bulk magnetic properties. Stealthy hyperuniform configurations are generated using generalized cos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of stealthy hyperuniform magnetic impurity configurations on bulk magnetism in a 2D Heisenberg model.
motivation: To understand how different spatial arrangements of magnetic impurities influence the magnetic properties of quantum antiferromagnets.
method: The authors generate stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations using generalized cosine functions and perform numerical simulations on the Heisenberg model.
result: Stealthy hyperuniform configurations lead to distinct bulk magnetic behavior compared to random configurations, affecting the magnetization and correlation functions.
conclusion: Impurity spatial correlations significantly impact bulk magnetism, and stealthy hyperuniformity offers a new way to engineer magnetic properties.

title: Multiple Quasiparticle Bound States In A Local Superconducting Gap Variation
authors: Romy Morin, Denis M. Basko, Manuel Houzet, And Julia S. Meyer
abstract:
Author(s): Romy Morin, Denis M. Basko, Manuel Houzet, and Julia S. Meyer

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024501] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiple quasiparticle bound states in a local superconducting gap variation, focusing on dissipation in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Excess quasiparticles in superconducting circuits cause dissipation, degrading device performance; understanding their dynamics is crucial.
method: The authors theoretically analyze quasiparticle bound states in a spatially varying superconducting gap using a microscopic model.
result: They find multiple bound states and characterize their energies and wavefunctions.
conclusion: The results help explain quasiparticle dynamics and dissipation in superconducting devices.

title: Superconducting State With Broken Time-reversal Symmetry And Collective Modes In The Kagome Superconductors $A{\mathrm{V}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$ ($A=\mathrm{K}$, Cs, Rb)

tldr: This paper studies unconventional pairing and collective modes in kagome superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry.
motivation: To understand the superconducting state and collective excitations in the recently discovered kagome superconductors AV3Sb5.
method: The authors solve gap equations at zero temperature and analyze collective modes within a multiband model.
result: They identify a transition from normal s-wave pairing to a state with broken time-reversal symmetry and characterize the associated collective modes.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the unconventional superconductivity in kagome materials.

title: Raman Response Of Collective Modes In Multicomponent Superconductors
authors: Yuki Yamazaki And Takahiro Morimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Yamazaki and Takahiro Morimoto

We formulate a microscopic theory of the Raman response of superconducting collective modes in multicomponent superconductors. Starting from a general Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian with a separable pairing interaction, we derive a gauge-invariant expression for the Raman susceptibility, inc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034502] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory for Raman response of collective modes in multicomponent superconductors.
motivation: Understanding collective modes in multicomponent superconductors is important for characterizing their properties, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors start from a Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian with separable pairing interaction and derive a gauge-invariant expression for the Raman susceptibility.
result: They compute the Raman response of collective modes, including amplitude and phase modes, in multicomponent superconductors.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for interpreting Raman experiments on multicomponent superconductors, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Continuum Fractons: Quantization And The Few-body Problem
authors: Ylias Sadki, Abhishodh Prakash, And S. L. Sondhi
abstract:
Author(s): Ylias Sadki, Abhishodh Prakash, and S. L. Sondhi

We formulate a continuum quantum mechanics for nonrelativistic, dipole-conserving fractons. Imposing symmetries and locality results in novel phenomena absent in ordinary quantum mechanical systems. A single fracton has a vanishing Hamiltonian, and thus its spectrum is entirely composed of zero mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a continuum quantum mechanics for dipole-conserving fractons, revealing novel phenomena such as a vanishing single-fracton Hamiltonian.
motivation: Fractons are exotic quasiparticles with restricted mobility due to dipole conservation, and a continuum formulation is needed to understand their quantum behavior beyond lattice models.
method: The authors impose symmetries and locality to construct a continuum quantum field theory for nonrelativistic, dipole-conserving fractons, analyzing the few-body problem.
result: They find that a single fracton has a vanishing Hamiltonian, leading to a spectrum of zero modes, and that two-fracton interactions produce bound states with unusual properties.
conclusion: The continuum approach reveals fundamentally new quantum mechanical features of fractons, but the work is primarily a theoretical study of a condensed matter system without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Competitive Orders In Altermagnetic Chiral Magnons
authors: Congzhe Yan, Zhijun Jiang, Jinyang Ni, And Guoqing Chang
abstract:

The magnons in altermagnets exhibit chiral splitting even in the absence of spin-orbit coupling and external magnetic fields. [Phys. Rev. B 114, L020401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral splitting of magnons in altermagnets at finite temperature, focusing on magnetic order competition.
motivation: To understand the finite-temperature dynamics of chiral magnons in altermagnets, which exhibit chiral splitting without spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly numerical simulations to analyze the temperature dependence of chiral splitting and competing magnetic orders.
result: They find that chiral splitting persists at finite temperatures but is influenced by competing magnetic orders.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermal behavior of altermagnetic chiral magnons, relevant for spintronics but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Majorana Zero Modes And Topological Nature In The ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ta}}_{3}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$ Family Of Superconductors

result: The materials exhibit nontrivial band topology and support Majorana zero modes.
conclusion: The Bi2Ta3S6 family is a promising platform for topological superconductivity and Majorana physics.

title: Anharmonic Superconducting Density Functional Theory: A General Framework For Superconductivity With Anharmonic Corrections
authors: Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, And Yipeng An

First-principles studies of superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects (AHE), despite their crucial role in achieving quantitative accuracy in many materials. To bridge this gap, we introduce a general computational approach, termed anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SC…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214521] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a computational framework (ah-SCDFT) that incorporates anharmonic effects into first-principles studies of superconductivity.
motivation: Standard first-principles methods for superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects, which are crucial for quantitative accuracy in many materials.
method: The authors develop an anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SCDFT) approach that includes anharmonic corrections to the electron-phonon coupling and phonon spectra.
result: The framework is demonstrated on several materials, showing improved agreement with experimental critical temperatures compared to standard SCDFT.
conclusion: ah-SCDFT provides a general and accurate method for predicting superconducting properties in materials where anharmonic effects are significant.

title: Reexamining The Strange Metal Charge Response With Transmission Inelastic Electron Scattering
authors: Niels de Vries, Eric Hoglund, Dipanjan Chaudhuri, Sang Hyun Bae, Jin Chen, Xuefei Guo, David Bałut, Genda Gu, Pinshane Huang, Jordan Hachtel, And Peter Abbamonte

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235158] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the charge response of strange metals using transmission inelastic electron scattering, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: Strange metals are a major unsolved problem in condensed matter physics, and understanding their charge susceptibility is key to developing theories like marginal Fermi liquid phenomenology.
method: The authors use transmission inelastic electron scattering to measure the momentum- and frequency-dependent charge susceptibility of a strange metal.
result: The paper provides experimental data on the charge response, which may inform theoretical models of strange metals.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the characterization of strange metals but do not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Layer-dependent Orbital Magnetization In graphene-Haldane Heterostructures
authors: Sovan Ghosh And Bheema Lingam Chittari
abstract:

Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) proximity coupled to a Haldane substrate provides a platform to investigate the interplay between band topology, layer number, and electric-field control of orbital magnetism. Using a tight-binding model and the modern theory of orbital magnetization, we study …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235160] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital magnetization in rhombohedral multilayer graphene proximity-coupled to a Haldane substrate, focusing on band topology and layer-dependent effects.
motivation: To understand the interplay between band topology, layer number, and electric-field control of orbital magnetism in graphene-based heterostructures.
method: Uses a tight-binding model and the modern theory of orbital magnetization to compute the orbital magnetic moment and magnetization as a function of layer number and electric field.
result: Finds that orbital magnetization exhibits strong layer dependence and can be tuned via electric field, with topological transitions occurring at certain layer numbers.
conclusion: The system provides a platform for controlling orbital magnetism through layer number and electric field, relevant for spintronics and valleytronics applications.

tldr: This paper studies edge states in a kagome lattice under various conditions using tight-binding methods.
motivation: To understand how lattice termination, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order affect edge state properties in kagome lattices.
method: Tight-binding model calculations for a two-dimensional kagome lattice with different boundary geometries and parameters.
result: Edge state existence and properties are highly sensitive to boundary geometry, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into topological edge states in kagome systems but are not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: The authors study a classical bilayer Ising model with moiré-modulated interlayer coupling, generated by relative twist or differential strain.
result: The model exhibits spatially modulated magnetic textures due to the moiré pattern.
conclusion: The work provides insights into moiré magnetism but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: Understanding the orbital magnetic moment of quasiparticles in superconductors is important for characterizing their response to magnetic fields.
method: The authors use a semiclassical wave packet approach, considering energy correction to linear order in magnetic field, to derive the orbital magnetic moment.
result: They obtain an expression for the orbital magnetic moment of Bogoliubov quasiparticles in terms of Berry curvature and other band structure quantities.
conclusion: The semiclassical theory provides a framework to compute orbital magnetic moments in superconductors, which may be relevant for transport and thermodynamic properties.

title: Anyon Dispersion In Aharonov-Casher Bands And Implications For Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Zihan Yan, Qingchen Li, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), And Eslam Khalaf

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235155] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of dispersing anyons in fractional quantum anomalous Hall systems, focusing on twisted MoTe2.
motivation: Understanding anyon dispersion is crucial for realizing itinerant anyon phases, but previous models assumed flat bands; this work accounts for realistic band geometry.
method: The authors construct momentum-resolved Laughlin quasihole states in Aharonov-Casher bands and use a momentum-space Monte Carlo framework to compute quasihole energies and bandwidths.
result: They find that nonuniform quantum geometry and quasihole Berry phase lead to finite anyon dispersion, with bandwidths relevant to twisted MoTe2.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled route to study itinerant anyon phases and highlights the role of band geometry in anyon dynamics.

title: Magnetoexcitons And Massive Dirac Fermions In Monolayers Of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides In A High Magnetic Field
authors: Katarzyna Sadecka, Marek Korkusiński, Ludmiła Szulakowska, And Paweł Hawrylak

method: Uses an ab initio-parametrized massive Dirac fermion model including valley and spin degrees of freedom to compute the emission spectrum of magnetoexcitons.
result: Describes the emission spectrum and interactions between magnetoexcitons and quantum Hall states.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for magnetoexciton physics in TMDs, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Quasiparticle Lifetime In Geometric Quantum Critical Metals

motivation: Understanding how geometric properties of the Fermi surface affect quasiparticle dynamics in quantum critical metals.
method: The authors analyze a model of fermions with a Fermi surface that has inflection points, using field-theoretic techniques to compute the quasiparticle self-energy and lifetime.
result: They find that at the geometric quantum critical point, the quasiparticle lifetime exhibits anomalous scaling due to the vanishing curvature, leading to non-Fermi liquid behavior.
conclusion: Geometric quantum phase transitions can significantly alter quasiparticle properties, providing a new mechanism for non-Fermi liquid physics.

motivation: To understand the role of cerium's 4f electron in pressure-induced quantum criticality in heavy-fermion ferromagnets.
method: Combining core-level photoemission and polarized x-ray absorption spectroscopy with single-impurity Anderson model simulations.
result: Kondo hybridization admixes higher-lying crystal field states into a multiorbital ground state with 4f occupancy ~0.9, explaining the dynamical spin response.
conclusion: Kondo hybridization and multiorbital ground state are essential for modeling quantum criticality in this system.

method: The authors analyze angle-dependent magnetoresistance in models of underdoped cuprates, likely using band structure calculations or effective Hamiltonians to reproduce the Yamaji oscillations.
result: The paper provides a theoretical explanation for the Yamaji effect observed in underdoped cuprates, supporting the existence of small hole pockets.
conclusion: The study confirms that the Yamaji effect can be understood within existing models of cuprate physics, reinforcing the picture of hole pockets in the pseudogap phase.

authors: Meita Asami, Kentaroh Watanabe, And Masakazu Sugiyama

motivation: To provide a fundamental understanding of the Stokes shift by linking absorption and emission processes through the optoelectronic reciprocity relation.
method: The authors revisit the van Roosbroeck-Shockley relation and generalized Planck's law, applying the optoelectronic reciprocity relation to bridge absorption and emission spectra.
result: They derive a new interpretation of the Stokes shift based on the reciprocity relation, showing how it arises from the asymmetry between absorption and emission due to thermalization and other factors.
conclusion: The optoelectronic reciprocity relation offers a unified framework for understanding the Stokes shift, with implications for optoelectronic device design.

title: Can Machine Learning Truly Decode Phase Transitions? A Deep Dive Into The Ising Model With Competing Interactions

title: Effects Of Quenched Disorder In Three-dimensional Lattice ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Gauge Higgs Models

authors: R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We present a systematic numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations. The networks are constructed with a truncated power-law degree distribution, ensuring finite moments, and correlations are introduced via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations, focusing on phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding how degree-degree correlations affect phase transitions in complex networks is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors construct networks with a truncated power-law degree distribution and introduce correlations via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rewiring method, then perform Monte Carlo simulations of the Ising model.
result: They find that degree-degree correlations significantly shift the critical temperature and alter the nature of the phase transition.
conclusion: Degree-degree correlations are an important factor in determining the critical behavior of the Ising model on complex networks.

title: Supercritical Transition Of Yukawa Fluids Identified By Excess Entropy
authors: Ao Xu And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Xu and Yan Feng

Equilibrium molecular dynamical simulations of three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa fluids are performed to investigate thermodynamics and supercritical transition of 3D dusty plasma fluids. The normalized reduced excess entropy [MATH] of 3D Yukawa fluids (where …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical transition of Yukawa fluids using excess entropy, which is a topic in classical statistical mechanics and plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the supercritical state of matter is important for dusty plasma physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of three-dimensional Yukawa fluids are performed to compute the normalized reduced excess entropy.
result: The supercritical transition is identified via a change in the behavior of excess entropy as a function of temperature and density.
conclusion: Excess entropy can serve as a reliable indicator of the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.

title: From Geometry To Strategy: Symmetry Breaking In Cooperative Multiagent Active Dynamics
authors: Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, And Sergey Savel'ev
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, and Sergey Savel'ev

We investigate the emergence of cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems, where autonomous agents, modeled as active particles, learn to capture targets dynamically regenerated in geometrically distinct arenas. Using proximal policy optimization, we study ci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems using active particles, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how autonomous agents learn to cooperate or compete in dynamic environments with geometric constraints.
method: Uses proximal policy optimization (PPO) to train agents modeled as active particles in arenas with regenerating targets.
result: Agents exhibit symmetry-breaking and emergent strategies depending on arena geometry.
conclusion: Geometry can induce cooperative or competitive strategies in multiagent active systems.

title: Active Deformation Enhances Target Scanning In Crowded Two-dimensional Self-propelled Particle Simulations
authors: Lucas E. Wiebke And Daniel R. Parisi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas E. Wiebke and Daniel R. Parisi

Self-propelled particles (SPPs) model diverse transport phenomena, including T-cell motility within crowded lymph nodes. Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) by T cells remains poorly understood under dense conditions. Here we simulate a two-dimensional system of radius-oscillating …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active deformation in self-propelled particle simulations to enhance target scanning in crowded environments, applied to T-cell motility.
motivation: Understanding how T cells efficiently scan antigen-presenting cells in dense lymph nodes is poorly understood, and active deformation may improve scanning.
method: Two-dimensional simulations of radius-oscillating self-propelled particles are used to model T-cell motility and scanning efficiency.
result: Active deformation enhances target scanning in crowded conditions compared to non-deforming particles.
conclusion: Active deformation is a beneficial strategy for efficient scanning in dense environments, with implications for immune response modeling.

title: Nonclassical Interfacial Response In Ionic Liquids At Blocking Electrodes
authors: Mahdi Yavarian And Roderick Melnik
abstract:
Author(s): Mahdi Yavarian and Roderick Melnik

The linear response of a symmetric binary ionic liquid confined between two parallel, blocking electrodes is analyzed under the influence of electrostatic correlations [MATH] while systematically comparing the effects of two distinct interfacial boundary conditions: the Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev (B…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the linear response of ionic liquids between blocking electrodes, focusing on electrostatic correlations and boundary conditions.
motivation: Understanding the nonclassical interfacial response of ionic liquids is important for applications in energy storage and electrochemistry.
method: The authors analyze a symmetric binary ionic liquid model using linear response theory and compare two interfacial boundary conditions (Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev and another).
result: The analysis reveals how electrostatic correlations and boundary conditions affect the differential capacitance and charge distribution at the interface.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition significantly influences the predicted interfacial properties, highlighting the need for accurate models in ionic liquid systems.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks
authors: R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh
abstract:
Author(s): R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, and R. Suresh

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. The coupling strengths coevolve according to a Hebbian adaptation rule and self-organize to support a wide variety of collective states. We observe frequency-clu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) and Hebbian adaptation affect collective states in oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera-like states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration strength.
conclusion: Frustration induces a rich variety of collective dynamical states in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant to neural and biological systems.

title: Quantized Dynamical Pumping Via Dissipation In A Mechanical Thouless Pump
authors: Marius Jürgensen And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Marius Jürgensen and Mikael C. Rechtsman

Thouless pumps are time-periodic one-dimensional systems that capture the physics of the two-dimensional quantum Hall effect via the quantized pumping of particles under adiabatic modulation. Recent work in photonics has shown that nonlinearity can act to quantize the displacement of light in the fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064154] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantized dynamical pumping in a mechanical Thouless pump, focusing on the role of dissipation in stabilizing quantization.
motivation: Thouless pumps typically rely on adiabatic modulation, but dissipation can also lead to quantized transport; understanding this mechanism is important for topological pumping in open systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a mechanical Thouless pump model with dissipation, using Floquet theory and numerical simulations to compute the pumped charge.
result: They find that dissipation can induce quantized pumping even in the absence of adiabaticity, with the quantization protected by topology.
conclusion: Dissipation can serve as a resource for robust quantized transport in mechanical systems, extending the concept of Thouless pumping to non-Hermitian settings.

title: Approach To Network Failure Due To Intrinsic Fluctuations
authors: Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, And M. S. Santhanam
abstract:
Author(s): Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, and M. S. Santhanam

We investigate the asymptotic failure of the network arising solely from intrinsic fluctuations in the flux passing through its nodes. By modeling the flux as random walkers and the node failure induced by large fluctuations as extreme events, it is shown that three distinct nodal failure regimes ca…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062302] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies network failure due to intrinsic fluctuations in node flux, modeled as random walkers and extreme events.
motivation: Understanding how intrinsic fluctuations in network traffic can lead to node failures is important for network reliability.
method: The authors model flux as random walkers and treat large fluctuations as extreme events to analyze nodal failure regimes.
result: Three distinct nodal failure regimes are identified based on the statistics of fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting network failures arising from internal noise rather than external attacks.

title: Van Hove Singularities In The Density Of States Of A Chaotic Dynamical System
authors: Bryn Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Bryn Davies

We show that the statistics of chaotic systems can be predicted by constructing an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computing their densities of states. For such operators, the density of states is well understood and can be computed straightforwardly, often yielding explic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064211] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts chaotic system statistics using periodic differential operators and their density of states, revealing Van Hove singularities.
motivation: To understand the statistical properties of chaotic dynamical systems by linking them to well-understood periodic operators.
method: Constructs an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computes their densities of states.
result: The density of states exhibits Van Hove singularities, which can be used to predict chaotic system statistics.
conclusion: The approach provides a new way to analyze chaotic systems through spectral theory of periodic operators.

title: Controlling Synchronization Dynamics Via Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges. We propose a physics-informed neural network framework for continuous-time synchronization regulation, in which system trajectories and contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064212] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to control synchronization dynamics in networked systems.
motivation: Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges.
method: A physics-informed neural network framework is proposed for continuous-time synchronization regulation, incorporating system trajectories and control objectives into the loss function.
result: The framework enables precise control of synchronization timing and degree in networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a flexible and effective approach for synchronization control in complex networks.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor
authors: Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, And Subhadeep Datta
abstract:

Relaxation dynamics of supercooled liquids approaching glassy arrest remain a central challenge in integrated electronic architectures, where conventional rheometry becomes incompatible. Here, we demonstrate that an ambipolar [MATH] field-effect transistor functions as an electrical p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065425] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses an ambipolar transistor to probe the glass transition in supercooled ionic liquids, an experimental condensed matter physics study.
motivation: Conventional rheometry is incompatible with integrated electronic architectures, so an electronic method is needed to study relaxation dynamics near the glass transition.
method: An ambipolar field-effect transistor is fabricated with supercooled ionic liquids as the channel material, and its electrical transport properties are measured as a function of temperature.
result: The transistor characteristics reveal signatures of the glass transition, demonstrating electronic access to the relaxation dynamics.
conclusion: The ambipolar transistor platform can serve as a sensitive probe of glassy dynamics in ionic liquids, bridging electronic and rheological measurements.

title: Mode Coupling And Resonance-induced Relaxation In Carbon Nanotubes
authors: Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, And Liang Huang

Author(s): Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, and Liang Huang

Here we investigate the intrinsic relaxation dynamics of armchair carbon nanotubes (CNTs) under single-mode exci…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065507] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies vibrational mode relaxation in carbon nanotubes, focusing on thermal transport and mechanical coherence.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional materials is important for thermal management and nanomechanical resonator design.
method: The authors investigate intrinsic relaxation of armchair CNTs under single-mode excitation using theoretical modeling.
result: They find mode coupling and resonance-induced relaxation mechanisms that govern the decay of vibrational modes.
conclusion: The results provide insights into thermal transport and coherence control in carbon nanotubes.

title: Robustness Of Networks Of Hypergraphs
authors: Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, And Jie Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, and Jie Zhou

Hypergraphs provide a natural representation of complex systems with higher-order interactions and are commonly interdependent with each other. In this work, based on a bipartite network representation of hypergraphs, we propose a framework of networks of hypergraphs (NOH) to describe the structures…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064312] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for networks of hypergraphs to study robustness under node failures.
motivation: Real-world systems often involve interdependent hypergraphs, but existing models do not capture such structures.
method: The authors model hypergraphs as bipartite networks and define a network of hypergraphs (NOH) framework, then analyze robustness via percolation theory.
result: They derive analytical expressions for the critical threshold and giant component size in NOH under random node failures.
conclusion: The NOH framework reveals that interdependence between hypergraphs can significantly affect system robustness.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Organic Mixed Conductors: Phase Transitions In A Lattice Gas
authors: Lukas M. Bongartz
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Bongartz

Organic mixed conductors (OMCs) represent a promising class of materials for applications in bioelectronics, physical computing, and thermoelectrics. Rather unparalleled, OMCs feature dynamics spanning multiple length and timescales, involving an intricate coupling between electronic, ionic, and mas…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065424] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in a lattice gas model for organic mixed conductors, focusing on statistical mechanics of ionic and electronic coupling.
motivation: Organic mixed conductors have complex dynamics spanning multiple scales; understanding their statistical mechanics is crucial for applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics.
method: The author develops a lattice gas model incorporating electronic, ionic, and mass transport degrees of freedom, and analyzes phase transitions using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations.
result: The model predicts several phase transitions driven by the interplay between electronic and ionic degrees of freedom, with implications for conductivity and thermoelectric performance.
conclusion: The lattice gas model captures essential physics of organic mixed conductors, providing a framework for understanding their thermodynamic behavior and guiding material design.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation of biomolecular condensates in confined spaces, focusing on the effect of finite molecule numbers.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the impact of confinement and finite molecule numbers on surface phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for phase separation near a surface in a confined system with a finite number of molecules, likely using statistical mechanics or mean-field theory.
result: The study reveals how surface phase separation is influenced by confinement and finite-size effects, providing phase diagrams and scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Surface phase separation in confined spaces exhibits distinct features from bulk phase separation, which may be relevant for understanding cellular organization.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:

By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral operators in tight-binding models using Markov inequality bounds.
motivation: Efficient computation of local observables in large tight-binding models is computationally expensive; a linear-scaling method is needed.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error, enabling linear-scaling estimation of local spectral operators.
result: The method achieves linear scaling with system size and provides rigorous error bounds, demonstrated on graphene nanoribbons.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical tool for computing local observables in large systems, but is specific to tight-binding models and not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu
abstract:

As a nontrivial state of solid, Schwarz crystal manifests itself in extremely refined nanograins and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) grain boundaries, and therefore exceptional thermal and mechanical stability. However, it remains unexploited how the structural units interact and thermal tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the structural and thermal confinement of Schwarz crystals, a type of nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries.
motivation: Schwarz crystals exhibit exceptional thermal and mechanical stability, but the interaction of structural units and thermal transport mechanisms are not well understood.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to investigate the structural dynamics and thermal properties of Schwarz crystals.
result: They find that the unique nanograin structure and TPMS boundaries lead to suppressed thermal conductivity and enhanced stability.
conclusion: The confinement effects in Schwarz crystals provide a new route to engineer materials with tailored thermal properties.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala

Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the aging dynamics of topologically constrained ring polymers is important for polymer physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of dense ring-polymer systems with varying stiffness are performed to monitor dynamical arrest after instantaneous thermal quenches.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with increased stiffness leading to slower dynamics and more pronounced aging effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the glassy behavior of ring polymers, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Arbitrary Control Of non-Hermitian Skin Modes Via Disorder And An Electric Field
authors: Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, And Franco Nori

tldr: This paper studies the control of non-Hermitian skin modes using disorder and electric fields, focusing on non-Hermitian physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate in higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems is a major challenge.
method: The authors propose using disorder and electric fields to arbitrarily control the localization of non-Hermitian skin modes.
result: They demonstrate that skin modes can be manipulated to localize at desired boundaries or positions.
conclusion: This work provides a method for controlling non-Hermitian skin effects, which may have applications in wave manipulation but is not directly relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Engineering Magnetotransport Through Hierarchical Symmetry In Weyl Semimetal Superlattices
authors: Nathan C. Drucker, Federico Balduini, Jules Schadt, Lorenzo Rocchino, Tathagata Paul, Vicky Hasse, Claudia Felser, Heinz Schmid, Cezar B. Zota, And Bernd Gotsmann

Superlattice engineering, the introduction of periodic potentials to a material, can induce selective scattering events that modify the electrical properties of the material in predictable ways. Extending superlattice engineering to three-dimensional (3D) electronic materials can expand the tunabili…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033023] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetotransport in Weyl semimetal superlattices, focusing on symmetry-induced scattering effects.
motivation: To explore how periodic potentials in 3D materials can tune electrical properties via selective scattering.
method: The authors engineer superlattices in Weyl semimetals and measure magnetotransport to probe hierarchical symmetry effects.
result: They demonstrate controllable modification of transport properties through superlattice engineering.
conclusion: Superlattice engineering is a viable method for tailoring electronic properties in topological semimetals.

title: Adversarial Vulnerability Of Machine-learning Surrogates For Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, And Jun-Jie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, and Jun-Jie Zhang

Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), yet their robustness to small, structured input perturbations remains insufficiently characterized. Conventional adversarial training is largely impractical for artificial intelligence for CFD (AI4CFD…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial vulnerability of machine-learning surrogates for computational fluid dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate CFD, but their robustness to small input perturbations is not well characterized.
method: The authors likely apply adversarial attacks to ML-based CFD surrogates and evaluate their vulnerability.
result: The paper finds that ML surrogates for CFD are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations.
conclusion: Adversarial robustness should be considered when deploying ML surrogates in CFD applications.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on the transverse-field Ising model, showing accurate excitation energies.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach can efficiently compute quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Extended Hot-electron Model And Current Bistability In Insulating $a\text{−}{\mathrm{Y}}_{x}{\mathrm{Si}}_{1\text{−}x}$ Films
authors: Le Hong Hoàng To, Andrés M. Somoza, Shamashis Sengupta, Louis Dumoulin, Laurent Bergé, Stefanos Marnieros, Claire Akiko Marrache-Kikuchi, And Miguel Ortuño

Electron-phonon interactions play a central role in determining charge and heat transport in condensed matter systems, but in disordered and low-dimensional materials, this coupling can be strongly suppressed, leading to nontrivial transport phenomena. tldr: This paper studies electron-phonon interactions and current bistability in disordered insulating films, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding electron-phonon coupling in disordered materials is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend a hot-electron model to describe transport in amorphous YxSi1-x films and analyze current bistability.
result: They find that suppressed electron-phonon coupling leads to nontrivial transport phenomena including bistability.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but is not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Local Probe Evidence Supporting Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, And Z. Guguchia

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: To provide local probe evidence supporting the predicted altermagnetic state in Co1/4NbSe2, which has been suggested by neutron diffraction.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on single crystals of Co1/4NbSe2 to probe the magnetic properties at the microscopic level.
result: The μSR data reveal a clear signature of magnetic order consistent with altermagnetism, supporting the altermagnetic interpretation.
conclusion: The study confirms altermagnetism in Co1/4NbSe2 using a local probe, adding to the understanding of this novel magnetic phase.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, And Carsten Timm
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, and Carsten Timm

Locally noncentrosymmetric materials are attracting significant attention due to the unique phenomena associated with sublattice degrees of freedom. The recently discovered heavy-fermion superconductor [MATH] has emerged as a compelling example of this class, garnerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023363] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in CeRh2As2, a heavy-fermion superconductor.
motivation: To understand the unique superconducting phases arising from local noncentrosymmetry in CeRh2As2.
method: The authors use a theoretical model based on the two-sublattice structure and analyze the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and magnetic fluctuations.
result: They find that composite superconducting orders, including spin-triplet components, can emerge and compete with magnetism.
conclusion: The results explain the observed phase diagram and highlight the role of sublattice degrees of freedom in heavy-fermion superconductors.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Phase-space Methods For Near-resonant Light Propagation
authors: Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, and Gerd Leuchs

We study the dynamics of light interacting with a near-resonant atomic medium using the truncated Wigner and positive [MATH] phase-space representations. By mapping the atomic degrees of freedom via the Jordan-Schwinger transformation, we first analyze the system under unitary evolution before extendin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023353] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks phase-space methods for simulating near-resonant light propagation through atomic media.
motivation: To evaluate the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares the two phase-space methods under unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: The positive P representation remains accurate for longer times and stronger nonlinearities, while the truncated Wigner approximation fails in these regimes.
conclusion: Phase-space methods can be effective for simulating near-resonant light propagation, but care must be taken in choosing the appropriate representation for the parameter regime.

title: Correlated Many-body Quantum Dynamics Of The Peregrine Soliton
authors: D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, And S. I. Mistakidis

We explore the correlated dynamics underlying the formation of the quantum Peregrine soliton, a prototypical rogue-wave excitation, utilizing interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in an ultracold bosonic gas confined in a one-dimensional box trap. The latter emulates the so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023355] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the correlated many-body quantum dynamics of the Peregrine soliton in an ultracold bosonic gas.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of rogue-wave excitations, specifically the Peregrine soliton, in a controlled ultracold atomic system.
method: The authors perform interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in a one-dimensional box trap and analyze the resulting correlated dynamics using numerical simulations.
result: They observe the formation and dynamics of the quantum Peregrine soliton, revealing its correlated many-body nature.
conclusion: The study provides insights into quantum rogue-wave phenomena and their underlying many-body correlations.

title: Localization And Topological Signatures Under Periodic Twisting
authors: James Walkling, Antonio Štrkalj, And F. Nur Ünal
abstract:
Author(s): James Walkling, Antonio Štrkalj, and F. Nur Ünal

We theoretically explore a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions formed by superimposing two square-lattice potentials. Motivated by the rich physics emerging at different twist angles between the two lattices at equilibrium, we introduce periodic twisting by continuous…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023356] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions with periodic twisting, focusing on localization and topological signatures.
motivation: To explore the rich physics emerging from twist angles between two square lattices in a dynamical setting, extending equilibrium moiré systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-dimensional Aubry-André model with periodic twisting, likely using numerical simulations or analytical methods to study localization and topology.
result: The paper identifies localization and topological signatures under periodic twisting, but the abstract does not specify concrete findings.
conclusion: The work provides insights into dynamical moiré systems, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not evident.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, and Claude Ederer

We establish a quantitative relation between the altermagnetic spin splitting and different higher-order multipoles of the charge and magnetization density around the magnetic atoms. Magnetic multipoles such as octupoles or triakontadipoles have been suggested as potential ferroic order parameters f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023357] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative relation between altermagnetic spin splitting and higher-order multipoles of charge and magnetization density.
motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting is a key phenomenon in condensed matter physics, and identifying order parameters for it is important for understanding and controlling magnetic materials.
method: The authors derive a quantitative relation linking the spin splitting to magnetic multipoles such as octupoles and triakontadipoles, using symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: They show that specific higher-order multipoles serve as quantitative order parameters for the altermagnetic spin splitting, providing a direct connection between electronic structure and multipolar moments.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for characterizing altermagnetic materials using multipolar order parameters, which may aid in the design of spintronic devices.

title: Gapless Edge Gravitons And Quasiparticles In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems With Nonlocal Confinement
authors: Daniel Spasic-Mlacak And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Spasic-Mlacak and Nigel R. Cooper

Motivated by polaritonic platforms, this work investigates how nonlocal confinement affects the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems. It is found that the conventional edge modes are lost, to be replaced by new modes arising from bulk excitations—such as the graviton and quasielectron—that become gapless at the boundary.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022063] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies edge physics in fractional quantum Hall systems with nonlocal confinement, finding gapless edge gravitons and quasiparticles.
motivation: Motivated by polaritonic platforms, the authors investigate how nonlocal confinement alters the edge modes of fractional quantum Hall systems.
method: Theoretical analysis of edge excitations in fractional quantum Hall systems under nonlocal confinement conditions.
result: Conventional edge modes are replaced by gapless bulk excitations such as gravitons and quasielectrons at the boundary.
conclusion: Nonlocal confinement fundamentally changes the edge physics, leading to new gapless modes from bulk excitations.

title: Modulation Of High-energy Electrons With A Nanopore Matter Lens
authors: Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, And Changlin Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, and Changlin Zheng

We demonstrate the modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanosized pore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens. The inner Coulomb potential of matter decreases rapidly from the edge of the pore toward the center, creating a strong electric field on the order of 10 GV/m. This electric field st…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023345] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanopore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens.
motivation: To explore a new method for focusing and modulating high-energy electron beams using nanoscale structures.
