method: The authors use a nanosized pore in a solid material, where the inner Coulomb potential creates a strong electric field (∼10 GV/m) to act as an electrostatic lens for high-energy electrons.
result: They show that the nanopore can effectively modulate the trajectory of high-energy electrons, achieving focusing effects.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a novel approach for electron beam manipulation, with potential applications in electron microscopy and lithography.

title: Theory Uncertainties In Predictions Of Strong-field Qed
authors: T. G. Blackburn
abstract:
Author(s): T. G. Blackburn

Experiments using high-power lasers and relativistic electron beams will soon be capable of precision testing of the theory of strong-field quantum electrodynamics. The comparison between experiment and theory always occurs via numerical simulations, but the lack of quantitative uncertainty bounds f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023346] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses theoretical uncertainties in numerical simulations of strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) for high-power laser experiments.
motivation: Precision tests of strong-field QED require accurate simulations, but quantitative uncertainty bounds are lacking.
method: The author analyzes sources of uncertainty in numerical simulations of strong-field QED processes.
result: The paper identifies and quantifies various theoretical uncertainties affecting predictions.
conclusion: Understanding these uncertainties is crucial for reliable comparison between experiment and theory in strong-field QED.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, highlighting the importance of rare events.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous complexity proofs for BosonSampling only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; this gap needed to be bridged.
method: The authors prove that approximate sampling from the output distribution of linear-optical networks with a linear number of modes is hard for classical computers under standard complexity assumptions.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard, extending the theoretical basis to the regime relevant for near-term experiments.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for photonic quantum advantage experiments in the saturated regime.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks and analyze training instabilities.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning and identifies ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The work contributes to machine learning theory but is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantization of chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations that can be detected via neutron scattering.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for detecting chiral solitons via inelastic neutron scattering.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a novel numerical approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs on a sphere, and analyze the spectrum and correlation functions.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a powerful tool for studying 3D fermionic CFTs and reveals emergent symmetries that are not manifest in the Lagrangian.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré superstructures is important for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures for potential applications in information processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for engineering robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that uses physical principles to infer causal relationships from time-series data of networked systems.
result: The framework successfully predicts links across various networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a physics-based tool for network inference with broad applicability.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices, which is important for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect while preserving time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect without an external magnetic field.
conclusion: This work provides a framework for realizing superconducting diodes in gate-defined homojunctions, with potential applications in low-power electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: Provides a robust mechanism for engineering anyonic exciton superfluids in quantum Hall bilayers.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits exotic magnetic behavior.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other characterization techniques.
result: Observation of a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and evidence for hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic properties of kagome spin ice systems and the role of universality classes in frustrated magnets.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands require cryogenic temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature stable platform.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT).
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, with tunability via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics at room temperature, potentially enabling practical applications.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, and to demonstrate control over its quantum anomalous Hall state.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic phases under varying electric and magnetic fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control enables transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the physics of twisted bilayer WSe2 and demonstrates a platform for exploring topological phases and magnetic order in moiré systems.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, and their critical behavior at the liquid-vapor transition is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly simulations to analyze the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids remain unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid-vapor critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the critical behavior of hyperuniform systems, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of full transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on the structural and dielectric properties of these materials.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex behavior that is not fully understood; understanding the nematic ordering may help explain their unique properties.
method: The authors use experimental techniques and theoretical modeling to characterize the dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic phase and describe its impact on the material's dielectric response.
conclusion: The dipolar nematic state is a key feature of relaxor ferroelectrics, and its study advances the understanding of these materials.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, challenging the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To investigate whether the thermodynamic limit assumption holds in quantum spin and dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific domain shapes and analyze ground state properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can lead to different macroscopic ground states, indicating a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation can invalidate the thermodynamic limit in certain quantum spin and dimer models.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the non-equilibrium dynamics and hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe excitations.
result: Discovery of a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable states with distinct properties in manganites.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; quantum speedups could enable analysis of larger datasets.
method: The paper designs a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological invariants to compute persistence diagrams.
result: The algorithm achieves provable exponential speedup over classical methods for certain input classes.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential quantum advantage in a practical data analysis task, but the topic is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing applications is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing, but lacks specific technical contributions.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with optical fluorescence, using the tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding 2D magnetism and its potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on their exotic electronic states and many-body phenomena.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual states in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and orbital antiferromagnetism.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic band structures, correlation effects, and topological properties.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and amplified anomalous Hall effects.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic states, with potential for new physics.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theory.
method: The authors present a pedagogical review of field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, applied to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic techniques can handle chemical systems and have applications in ecology and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful unified framework for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and x-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide crucial information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and x-ray pulse profile measurements, and compares them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials such as α-RuCl3, with emphasis on chiral edge modes and topological properties.
result: Summarizes key candidate materials and their topological properties, including evidence for chiral edge modes.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising materials, but further experimental confirmation is needed.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, covering all facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review presents an outlook on how these models can be incorporated into studies relevant to applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature and can be applied to practical photonic and energy harvesting systems.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum effects such as tunneling, superposition, and entanglement in skyrmion systems, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to test fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental approaches, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review catalogs current constraints on various exotic boson couplings and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a promising avenue for probing physics beyond the standard model, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental limits, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made under conditions that violate the assumptions of the bounds, and shows how designed materials can exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds do not contradict thermodynamics but rather highlight the importance of assumptions; this understanding can guide development of materials with superior properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of quantum many-body systems in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Survey of atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms for realizing nonstandard geometries, including synthetic dimensions and curved lattices.
result: Summarizes recent progress in engineering fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional quantum matter.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new avenues for studying fundamental physics but are not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental systems, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with broad implications for future discoveries and applications.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review explores the intersection of quantum mechanics and gravity using massive quantum systems as probes.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental approaches for testing gravity-induced decoherence, collapse, and entanglement.
result: It surveys ongoing experiments that aim to detect gravitational effects on quantum systems, such as matter-wave interferometry and entanglement generation.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but the field is still in early stages with no definitive results yet.

title: General-Purpose Inverse Design Of Heterogeneous Finite-Sized Assemblies
authors: Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, And Michael P. Brenner
abstract:
Author(s): Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, and Michael P. Brenner

Designing heterogeneous, self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology. We present a framework that uses gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning systems toward target equilibrium yields. We design systems ranging from simple dimers to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018201] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a gradient-based optimization framework for inverse design of heterogeneous self-assembling systems to achieve target equilibrium yields.
motivation: Designing heterogeneous self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology; the authors aim to provide a general-purpose method to tune such systems toward desired yields.
method: The framework uses gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, allowing systematic design of assemblies ranging from simple dimers to more complex structures.
result: The approach successfully designs systems with target equilibrium yields, demonstrating its applicability to various heterogeneous assemblies.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a general and efficient method for inverse design of self-assembling systems, with potential applications in soft matter and biology.

title: Electron-molecule Scattering Via $R$-matrix Variational Algorithms On A Quantum Computer
authors: Dario Picozzi, Jonathan Tennyson, Vincent Graves, And Jimena D. Gorfinkiel
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Picozzi, Jonathan Tennyson, Vincent Graves, and Jimena D. Gorfinkiel

Electron-molecule collisions play a central role in both natural processes and modern technological applications, particularly in plasma processing. Conventional computational strategies such as the [MATH]-matrix method have been widely adopted yet encounter significant scaling challenges in treating m…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012407] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using quantum computers to accelerate electron-molecule scattering calculations via the R-matrix method.
motivation: Electron-molecule collisions are important for plasma processing but classical R-matrix methods face scaling challenges for large molecules.
method: The authors develop variational quantum algorithms to solve the R-matrix equations on a quantum computer.
result: They demonstrate the approach on small molecules and show potential for quantum advantage in treating larger systems.
conclusion: Quantum computing may enable efficient electron-molecule scattering simulations that are classically intractable.

title: Engineering The Geometric Optics Limit Of Wave-packet Reflection From A Planar Interface
authors: Sajjad Bashiri, Yahong Chen, And Sergey A. Ponomarenko
abstract:
Author(s): Sajjad Bashiri, Yahong Chen, and Sergey A. Ponomarenko

A phase-space nonseparable light beam can be tuned so that the Goos-Hänchen and Imbert-Fedorov shifts induced by reflection from a simple metal interface vanish at the same incidence angle. This Letter shows how spatial coherence, phase-space twist, and polarization provide practical control knobs for approaching a geometric-optics reflection limit with standard metallic coatings.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011501] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates how to engineer the Goos-Hänchen and Imbert-Fedorov shifts of a partially coherent light beam to vanish at a planar interface, approaching the geometric optics limit.
motivation: The Goos-Hänchen and Imbert-Fedorov shifts cause deviations from geometric optics at interfaces; eliminating them is desirable for precision applications.
method: The authors use a phase-space nonseparable (twisted) light beam and tune its spatial coherence, twist, and polarization to cancel both shifts simultaneously at a metal interface.
result: They show that with appropriate beam parameters, both shifts can be made to vanish at the same incidence angle, achieving a geometric-optics-like reflection.
conclusion: Spatial coherence and polarization provide practical control knobs to approach the geometric optics limit with standard metallic coatings.

title: Ab Initio Modeling And Experimental Analysis Of Contrast In Broadband Coherent anti-Stokes Raman Spectroscopy: A Case Study On Ferroelectric Domain Walls
authors: Robin Buschbeck, Mike N. Pionteck, Naomi Herrmann, Michael Rüsing, Susanne C. Kehr, Simone Sanna, And Lukas M. Eng
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Buschbeck, Mike N. Pionteck, Naomi Herrmann, Michael Rüsing, Susanne C. Kehr, Simone Sanna, and Lukas M. Eng

Raman imaging, based on incoherent spontaneous Raman scattering (SR) or coherent techniques such as broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (BCARS), is a powerful tool for visualizing local lattice distortions. It can thus be employed, e.g., to identify and visualize ferroelectric (FE) dom…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034104] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio modeling and experimental BCARS analysis of ferroelectric domain walls, focusing on contrast mechanisms in Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand and predict contrast in BCARS imaging of ferroelectric domain walls, which is important for characterizing local lattice distortions.
method: Combines density functional theory (DFT) calculations of Raman tensors with experimental BCARS measurements on lithium niobate.
result: The modeling reproduces experimental contrast patterns and reveals the role of specific phonon modes in domain wall imaging.
conclusion: Ab initio modeling can reliably predict BCARS contrast, aiding interpretation of domain wall structures in ferroelectrics.

title: Anomalously Robust Fabry-Pérot Bound States In The Continuum In A Coupled Triple-resonator System
authors: Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, And Yong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, and Yong Li

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) with ultrahigh quality ([MATH]) factors hold great promise for enhancing wave–matter interactions. However, their practical realization is hindered by extreme fragility to structural imperfections. Here, we report an anomalously robust Fabry–Pérot (FP) BIC in a coup…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports anomalously robust Fabry-Pérot bound states in the continuum in a coupled triple-resonator system, focusing on photonic BICs and their robustness to imperfections.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are promising for enhancing wave-matter interactions but are typically fragile to structural imperfections; this work aims to find a robust BIC design.
method: The authors propose and analyze a coupled triple-resonator system that supports Fabry-Pérot BICs, using theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to study their robustness.
result: They demonstrate that the Fabry-Pérot BIC in this system is anomalously robust against structural perturbations, maintaining high quality factors even with imperfections.
conclusion: The robust BIC design could enable practical applications in photonics, such as lasers and sensors, where stability against fabrication errors is crucial.

title: Unveiling The Impact Of Cross-order Hyperdegree Correlations In Contagion Processes On Hypergraphs
authors: Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, And István Z. Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, and István Z. Kiss

Contagion processes in social systems often involve interactions that go beyond pairwise contacts. Higher-order networks, represented as hypergraphs, have been widely used to model multibody interactions, and their presence can drastically alter contagion dynamics compared to traditional network mod…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies contagion processes on hypergraphs, focusing on the impact of cross-order hyperdegree correlations.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions affect epidemic spreading is important for modeling social systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework to analyze contagion dynamics on hypergraphs with correlated hyperdegrees across different orders.
result: They find that cross-order correlations can significantly alter the epidemic threshold and outbreak size.
conclusion: The work contributes to network science and epidemiology, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Finite-size Scaling In Quasi-three-dimensional Stick Percolation
authors: Ryan K. Daniels
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan K. Daniels

This work extends the universal finite-size scaling framework for continuum percolation from two-dimensional (2D) to quasi-three-dimensional (Q3D) stick systems, in which sequentially deposited wires of finite diameter stack vertically on a flat substrate. Using Monte Carlo simulation, the percolati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size scaling in quasi-three-dimensional stick percolation using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding percolation in quasi-3D systems is important for applications like conductive nanowire networks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of sequentially deposited sticks with finite diameter on a flat substrate, analyzing percolation thresholds and scaling exponents.
result: Extends universal finite-size scaling framework from 2D to quasi-3D stick systems, providing scaling exponents and percolation thresholds.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical percolation theory but has no direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Higher-order Adaptive Behaviors Outperform Pairwise Strategies In Mitigating Contagion Dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, And Alain Barrat
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, and Alain Barrat

When exposed to a contagion phenomenon, individuals may respond to the perceived risk of infection by adopting behavioral changes, aiming to reduce their exposure or their risk of infecting others. The social cost of such adaptive behaviors and their impact on the contagion dynamics have been invest…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how higher-order adaptive behaviors (e.g., group-level responses) outperform pairwise strategies in mitigating contagion dynamics on networks.
motivation: Understanding how individual behavioral changes affect epidemic spread is crucial, but most models consider only pairwise interactions; higher-order effects may be important.
method: The authors develop a model of contagion with adaptive behaviors at different orders (individual, pairwise, and group) and analyze the dynamics using simulations and analytical approximations.
result: Higher-order adaptive behaviors are more effective at reducing the final epidemic size and peak prevalence compared to pairwise strategies, especially in dense networks.
conclusion: Incorporating higher-order social interactions in behavioral responses can significantly improve mitigation strategies for contagion processes.

title: Analytical Theory Of Chiral Active Particle Transport In A Fluctuating Density Field
authors: Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, And Shradha Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, and Shradha Mishra

We develop a closed-form analytical theory for the transport of a chiral active Brownian particle in three dimensions, moving through a fluctuating local density field that models steric and dynamical interactions in a dense active medium. The density field is modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck proces…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064155] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical theory for chiral active particle transport in a fluctuating density field, focusing on soft matter physics.
motivation: To understand transport properties of chiral active particles in dense active media, which is relevant to biological and soft matter systems.
method: Models the density field as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and derives closed-form expressions for transport coefficients using stochastic calculus.
result: Provides analytical expressions for mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficient as functions of chirality and density fluctuations.
conclusion: The theory captures the interplay between chirality and environmental fluctuations, offering predictions for experimental systems.

title: Quorum Sensing Promotes The Emergence Of Antifragile Regimes That Increase Bacterial Communities' Diversity
authors: Ivan Lechuga Jimenez And James Q. Boedicker
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Lechuga Jimenez and James Q. Boedicker

Understanding the mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition has implications in the ecology and evolution of both natural and synthetic microbial communities. Quorum sensing (QS), the regulation of cellular activity through signal exchange as a response to cell density, is a common mecha…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064411] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quorum sensing in bacterial communities promotes antifragile regimes that increase diversity, using a computational model.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition is important for ecology and evolution of microbial communities.
method: The authors develop a computational model of bacterial communities with quorum sensing and analyze the emergence of antifragile regimes and their effect on diversity.
result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.
conclusion: Quorum sensing can enhance community resilience and diversity through antifragile dynamics.

title: Stretched-exponential Aging Governs Nonequilibrium Precipitate Patterns
authors: Amari Z. Morris And Oliver Steinbock
abstract:
Author(s): Amari Z. Morris and Oliver Steinbock

Localized growth in driven materials is often governed by intermittent failure, yet how a material's history biases failure sites remains poorly understood. Using pause-restart experiments on chemical precipitate membranes, we quantify the probability of age-dependent breaching. We show that the kin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033025] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies aging and breaching in chemical precipitate membranes, a non-equilibrium pattern formation problem.
motivation: Understanding how material history biases failure sites in driven materials is poorly understood.
method: Pause-restart experiments on chemical precipitate membranes quantify the probability of age-dependent breaching.
result: Stretched-exponential aging governs the nonequilibrium precipitate patterns.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into intermittent failure in driven materials.

title: Hydrodynamic Attraction And Hindered Diffusion Govern First-passage Times Of Swimming Microorganisms
authors: Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, And Christina Kurzthaler
abstract:
Author(s): Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, and Christina Kurzthaler

Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall reveal how hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion shape first-passage-time statistics. The results show that wall-induced hindered diffusion can strongly delay wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction produces distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022060] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near a wall using numerical simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic attraction and hindered diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how microorganisms navigate near surfaces is important for biological and ecological processes, but the role of hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion on first-passage times is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion significantly affect the first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near walls, with implications for microbial ecology and biophysics.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan
abstract:
Author(s): Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, and Oleg Kogan

Time delay can have a significant impact on the properties of collective organization of active matter. In the previous paper [
tldr: This paper studies aging in a swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective dynamics of active matter.
motivation: Time delay can significantly impact collective organization in active matter systems, and understanding aging phenomena is important for biological and physical systems.
method: The authors extend a previous swarmalator model to include time-delayed interactions and analyze the resulting dynamics using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They find that time delay induces aging behavior, characterized by a gradual loss of synchronization and structural changes in the crystal.
conclusion: Time delay is a crucial factor in the aging dynamics of swarmalator crystals, providing insights into the collective behavior of active matter with delayed interactions.

title: Redirecting Countermoving Swarms Through Collision
authors: Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy Mcguire, And Ira B. Schwartz
abstract:
Author(s): Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy McGuire, and Ira B. Schwartz

Multiswarm systems, where two or more swarms of mobile agents occupy the same region of space with different parameters and goals, occur in a variety of biological, engineering, and defense applications. Composites of multiple swarms can produce hybrid spatiotemporal patterns, which compared to sing…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023351] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of two countermoving swarms that collide and redirect, focusing on pattern formation and control.
motivation: Understanding and controlling multiswarm systems is important for biological, engineering, and defense applications.
method: The authors model two swarms with different parameters and goals, analyze their collision dynamics, and propose a redirection strategy.
result: They identify hybrid spatiotemporal patterns and demonstrate that collisions can be used to redirect swarms.
conclusion: Collision-based redirection is a viable control mechanism for multiswarm systems.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques.
result: Applications include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles, sorting of biological cells, and pulling forces.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the multimessenger implications for astrophysics.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, and understanding their detection prospects and multimessenger connections is important for advancing our knowledge of dense matter and neutron star physics.
method: The paper reviews the current status and future detection capabilities of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the role of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys the potential astrophysical implications of detecting continuous gravitational waves, including insights into nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations combining gravitational waves and electromagnetic signals will be crucial for understanding the extreme environments of neutron stars.

title: Magnetism And Magnetoelastic Effect In The Two-dimensional Van Der Waals Multiferroic ${\mathrm{CuCrP}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$
authors: Jiasen Guo, Ryan P. Siebenaller, Michael A. Susner, Jiaqiang Yan, Zachary Morgan, And Feng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Jiasen Guo, Ryan P. Siebenaller, Michael A. Susner, Jiaqiang Yan, Zachary Morgan, and Feng Ye

The ordered moment direction in the van der Waals multiferroic CuCrPn itu diffraction of strain-tunable magnetism in this two-dimensional magnet.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper determines the magnetic structure and magnetoelastic coupling in the van der Waals multiferroic CuCrP2S6 using neutron diffraction.
motivation: The ordered moment direction in CuCrP2S6 was unresolved despite interest, and understanding its magnetic structure is crucial for magnetoelectric studies.
method: Neutron diffraction was used to determine the ground-state magnetic structure, and magnetic field measurements were performed to uncover magnetoelastic coupling.
result: The ordered moments align along the crystallographic a-axis with weak spin anisotropy, and a magnetoelastic coupling was observed.
conclusion: This work provides a basis for future magnetoelectric study and in situ diffraction of strain-tunable magnetism in this 2D magnet.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of collision finding in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting inherent hardness.
conclusion: Simple neural networks may be suitable for cryptographic applications requiring collision resistance.

title: Resolving Spin State Discrepancies Of Small Cationic Iron Clusters By Far-Infrared Vibrational Spectroscopy
authors: Kevin Anthony Kaw, Ozan Lacinbala, Deepak Pradeep, Joost M. Bakker, Ewald Janssens, Peter Lievens, And Piero Ferrari
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin Anthony Kaw, Ozan Lacinbala, Deepak Pradeep, Joost M. Bakker, Ewald Janssens, Peter Lievens, and Piero Ferrari

A technique combining spectroscopy and computational simulations allows the geometry and spin magnetic moment of iron nanoclusters to be determined more precisely.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses far-infrared vibrational spectroscopy and computational simulations to determine the geometry and spin magnetic moment of small cationic iron clusters.
motivation: Understanding the spin state and geometry of iron clusters is important for their magnetic properties, but the paper focuses on cluster physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Far-infrared vibrational spectroscopy combined with density functional theory calculations.
result: The technique resolves discrepancies in spin state assignments for small iron clusters.
conclusion: The combined spectroscopic and computational approach provides precise determination of cluster geometry and spin magnetic moment.

title: Direct Observation Of Structural Disorder Near Critical Point In ${\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$ Crystal
