authors: Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, And Lin Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, and Lin Zhou

Critical points (CPs) in ferroelectrics are known for their association with giant dielectric and electromechanical responses, yet their structural origin, especially in nonrelaxor systems, remains unclear. We combine in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-bas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies structural disorder near the critical point in BaTiO3 using in situ TEM and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the structural origin of giant dielectric and electromechanical responses at critical points in ferroelectrics.
method: Combined in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-based simulations.
result: Direct observation of structural disorder near the critical point.
conclusion: The structural disorder may explain the enhanced responses at critical points.

title: Real-Space Dynamic Electron Correlation In Beryllium
authors: Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, And Takeshi Egami
abstract:
Author(s): Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, and Takeshi Egami

The size of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium is about 2 Å, but it extends up to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, demonstrating that electron correlations are affected significantly by electron dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256402] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamic electron correlation in beryllium using inelastic X-ray scattering, revealing the size and energy dependence of the exchange-correlation hole.
motivation: Understanding electron correlation is fundamental to condensed matter physics, but this work focuses on the real-space dynamics of correlations in a specific material, not on quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use inelastic X-ray scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor of beryllium and reconstruct the exchange-correlation hole in real space as a function of energy transfer.
result: The exchange-correlation hole size is about 2 Å at low energy, extending to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, showing that electron correlations are significantly affected by electron dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides direct experimental insight into dynamic electron correlation, but it is a condensed matter physics result without connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Synthetic Spatiotemporal Plasmonic Vortices On Chip
authors: Qian Chen, Shuoshuo Zhang, Guoyu Xian, Haoqiang Hu, Xiaohua Wu, Xiaofei Wu, Jer-Shing Huang, Chen-Bin Huang, Jin-Hui Zhong, Yuquan Zhang, Xiaocong Yuan, Changjun Min, And Yanan Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Chen, Shuoshuo Zhang, Guoyu Xian, Haoqiang Hu, Xiaohua Wu, Xiaofei Wu, Jer-Shing Huang, Chen-Bin Huang, Jin-Hui Zhong, Yuquan Zhang, Xiaocong Yuan, Changjun Min, and Yanan Dai

Spatiotemporal vortices are polychromatic modes that intertwine orbital angular momentum in space and time. Here, we introduce a new class of such vortices, “spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices,” carrying nontrivial topological spin textures. They are generated by chronotopic interference of temporall…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256903] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces synthetic spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices on a chip, which are polychromatic modes carrying topological spin textures.
motivation: The authors aim to create a new class of spatiotemporal vortices in plasmonic systems, enabling on-chip manipulation of light with structured space-time properties.
method: They generate spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices via chronotopic interference of temporally and spatially structured light fields on a metallic surface.
result: The vortices exhibit nontrivial topological spin textures and are demonstrated on a chip platform.
conclusion: This work expands the concept of spatiotemporal vortices to plasmonics, offering potential for integrated photonic devices with structured light.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism
authors: Yichen Liu And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Liu and Cheng-Cheng Liu

The antiferroaxial state is emerging as an important ferroic order in condensed matter systems. Here, we establish antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a broadly prevalent, generic, and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism, in which antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions both induce alter…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256709] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism in condensed matter systems.
motivation: The antiferroaxial state is an important ferroic order, and the authors aim to show that it can induce altermagnetism, providing a new multiferroic mechanism.
method: The authors develop a microscopic theory linking antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions to altermagnetism.
result: They demonstrate that antiferroaxial altermagnetism is broadly prevalent and generic in condensed matter systems.
conclusion: This work identifies a new multiferroic mechanism that combines antiferroaxial order with altermagnetism.

title: Ab Initio Calculations Of The Electronic Structure Of ${\mathrm{Ac}}^{+}$
authors: Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, And Anastasia Borschevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, and Anastasia Borschevsky

Accurate spectroscopic investigations of the heaviest elements are inherently challenging, due to their short lifetimes and low production yields. Success of such measurements requires both dedicated experimental techniques and strong theoretical support. Laser resonance chromatography (LRC) is a pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012801] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio calculations of the electronic structure of Ac+ for laser resonance chromatography.
motivation: Accurate spectroscopic data for heavy elements like actinium are needed to support experimental measurements, which are challenging due to short lifetimes and low yields.
method: Multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock and relativistic coupled-cluster methods are used to compute energy levels and transition probabilities.
result: Theoretical predictions for energy levels and transition rates are provided, aiding in the interpretation of future LRC experiments.
conclusion: The calculations offer essential theoretical support for spectroscopic studies of Ac+ and demonstrate the feasibility of LRC for heavy elements.

title: High-precision Calculation Of Resonant Electronic Recombination And Resonant Transfer Excitation Cross Sections In Na-like ${\mathrm{Fe}}^{15+}$ Ions
authors: Wenliang He, Luyou Xie, Chengpeng Yang, Yulong Ma, And Chenzhong Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Wenliang He, Luyou Xie, Chengpeng Yang, Yulong Ma, and Chenzhong Dong

Large-scale level-by-level calculations have been systematically performed to obtain the [MATH]-shell resonant electronic recombination cross sections of [MATH] ions, using the relativistic configuration interaction method considering the complex electronic correlations, the Breit and QE…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012803] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates resonant electronic recombination cross sections for Na-like Fe15+ ions using relativistic configuration interaction.
motivation: Accurate cross sections are needed for modeling astrophysical and fusion plasmas.
method: Large-scale level-by-level relativistic configuration interaction calculations including Breit and QED corrections.
result: High-precision cross sections for K-shell resonant electronic recombination are obtained.
conclusion: The calculations provide reliable atomic data for plasma diagnostics.

title: Interface Effects Of Pb Films On ${\mathrm{TlBiSe}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{3}$ Topological Insulators
authors: Roberto Flammini, Oreste de Luca, Martina Casciaro, Tommaso Caruso, Fabio Biffoli, Daniela Pacilé, Khatira Z. Mehtiyeva, Ziya S. Aliev, Alexey Barinov, Alfonso Policicchio, Anastasia G. Ryabishchenkova, Fabio Ronci, Stefano Colonna, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Raffaele G. Agostino, Sergey V. Eremeev, and Marco Papagno

We present an experimental investigation of the Pb-induced changes on the electronic structure of selected topological insulators, namely, [MATH] and [MATH]. Using spatially resolved and surface-sensitive techniques, including micro-angle-resolved photo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interface effects of lead films on topological insulators TlBiSe2 and Bi2Se3 using surface-sensitive techniques.
motivation: Understanding how metal overlayers modify the electronic structure of topological insulators is important for potential applications in spintronics and quantum computing.
method: The authors used micro-angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and other surface-sensitive techniques to probe the electronic structure changes induced by Pb deposition.
result: They observed modifications in the topological surface states and band structure due to Pb adsorption and interface formation.
conclusion: The Pb overlayer significantly alters the electronic properties of the topological insulators, which must be considered for device integration.

title: Quantitative Thermodynamic Study Of Superconducting And Normal States In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$ Under Pressure
authors: T. Vasina, M. Pfeiffer, R. Borth, M. Nicklas, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, J.-P. Brison, E. Hassinger, G. Knebel, And D. Braithwaite
abstract:
Author(s): T. Vasina, M. Pfeiffer, R. Borth, M. Nicklas, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, J.-P. Brison, E. Hassinger, G. Knebel, and D. Braithwaite

Pressurized UTe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235159] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A specific heat study of UTe2 under pressure reveals enhanced electronic correlations and complex phase behavior.
motivation: To understand the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2 under pressure.
method: Quantitative specific heat measurements under hydrostatic pressure, analyzing the Sommerfeld coefficient and phase boundaries.
result: The Sommerfeld coefficient increases threefold with pressure, indicating enhanced electronic correlations, and the phase diagram shows multiple superconducting and magnetic phases.
conclusion: The study provides new insights into the complex interactions in UTe2, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Subexponential Growth Dynamics In Complex Systems: A Piecewise Power-law Model For The Diffusion Of New Words And Names
authors: Hayafumi Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Hayafumi Watanabe

A study of online language shows that niche terms—like the name of a narrowly popular music group—spread less quickly than mainstream words.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the diffusion of new words and names in online language using a piecewise power-law model, finding that niche terms spread more slowly than mainstream ones.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of language evolution and the spread of new terms in complex social systems.
method: The authors propose a piecewise power-law model to describe subexponential growth dynamics and fit it to empirical data on word and name usage from online sources.
result: Niche terms exhibit slower diffusion compared to mainstream terms, consistent with subexponential growth patterns.
conclusion: The piecewise power-law model effectively captures the diffusion dynamics of linguistic terms, highlighting differences between niche and mainstream adoption.

title: Effects Of Spatial Beam Coherence And Plasma Scale Length On Stimulated Raman Scattering And Two-plasmon Decay
authors: Chiharu Nakatsuji, Yuji Takagi, Gabriele Cristoforetti, Sota Matsuura, Takuya Honda, Daisuke Tanaka, Dimitri Batani, Takumi Sato, Shun Horimoto, Hideo Nagatomo, Yasuhiko Sentoku, Philippe D. Nicolaï, Kai Taketoshi, Naoki Yamagata, Norimasa Ozaki, Yasunobu Arikawa, Akifumi Yogo, Shinsuke Fujioka, And Keisuke Shigemori
abstract:
Author(s): Chiharu Nakatsuji, Yuji Takagi, Gabriele Cristoforetti, Sota Matsuura, Takuya Honda, Daisuke Tanaka, Dimitri Batani, Takumi Sato, Shun Horimoto, Hideo Nagatomo, Yasuhiko Sentoku, Philippe D. Nicolaï, Kai Taketoshi, Naoki Yamagata, Norimasa Ozaki, Yasunobu Arikawa, Akifumi Yogo, Shinsuke Fujioka, and Keisuke Shigemori

We present an experimental investigation demonstrating that the suppression of parametric instabilities in laser-plasma interactions under conditions relevant to direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, specifically backward stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) and two-plasmon decay (TPD), shows the e…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally investigates the suppression of stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay in laser-plasma interactions relevant to inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Parametric instabilities in laser-plasma interactions can degrade the performance of direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, so understanding how to suppress them is important.
method: The authors performed experiments varying spatial beam coherence and plasma scale length, measuring the resulting levels of backward stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay.
result: They found that increasing spatial beam coherence and adjusting plasma scale length can suppress these instabilities.
conclusion: Controlling beam coherence and plasma conditions offers a path to mitigate parametric instabilities in fusion experiments.

title: Opacity Predictions In Plasmas Under Stellar Conditions Using Deep Learning
authors: Djamel Benredjem And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Djamel Benredjem and Jean-Christophe Pain

The aim of this work is to predict the opacity of plasmas under stellar conditions. We focus on iron and nickel, as these elements have been extensively investigated both theoretically and experimentally. In certain regimes, notably under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium, calculating the spectral …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict plasma opacity under stellar conditions for iron and nickel.
motivation: Accurate opacity predictions are needed for stellar modeling, but calculations under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium are computationally expensive.
method: A deep learning model is trained on existing opacity data to predict spectral opacities for iron and nickel plasmas.
result: The deep learning approach provides fast and accurate opacity predictions compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: Deep learning can serve as an efficient tool for opacity calculations in astrophysical plasmas.

title: Elastic Instability-induced Symmetry Breaking In Confined Microcavities
authors: Kai Tian, Tongtong Zhu, Xiaoyu Xu, Zhaodong Ding, Jifeng Cui, And Chundong Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Tian, Tongtong Zhu, Xiaoyu Xu, Zhaodong Ding, Jifeng Cui, and Chundong Xue

This study investigates the evolution mechanism of elastic instability in a bilateral double-cavity channel through numerical simulations and microfluidic experiments. Depending on the Weissenberg number ([MATH]), the flow is categorized into three regimes: stable symmetric vortex structures at…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic instability and symmetry breaking in confined microcavities using numerical simulations and microfluidic experiments.
motivation: To understand the evolution mechanism of elastic instability in a bilateral double-cavity channel, which is relevant to fluid dynamics and microfluidics.
method: Numerical simulations and microfluidic experiments are used to analyze flow regimes based on the Weissenberg number.
result: Three flow regimes are identified: stable symmetric vortex structures, symmetry-breaking, and chaotic flows.
conclusion: The study provides insights into elastic instability-induced symmetry breaking in microcavities, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Selective Wave Transmission In Strongly Nonlinear Disordered Granular Chains
authors: João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, And Surajit Sen
abstract:
Author(s): João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, and Surajit Sen

Chains of 1000 granules in mutual contact, without precompression, and with random radii that follow a normal distribution are studied numerically. The standard deviation [MATH] controls the disorder level. The chains are subject to (i) a striker impact and (ii) an actuator that imposes band-limited wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065426] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave transmission in strongly nonlinear disordered granular chains under impact and band-limited white noise.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in disordered granular media is important for applications like impact mitigation and energy harvesting.
method: Numerical simulations of 1000-granule chains with random radii following a normal distribution, subjected to striker impact or actuator-imposed band-limited white noise.
result: Selective wave transmission is observed depending on disorder level and excitation type.
conclusion: Disorder in granular chains can be used to control wave transmission properties.

title: Geomimicry: Emergent Dynamics In Earth-mediated Complex Materials
authors: Shravan Pradeep, Emanuela Del Gado, Douglas J. Jerolmack, And Paulo E. Arratia
abstract:
Author(s): Shravan Pradeep, Emanuela Del Gado, Douglas J. Jerolmack, and Paulo E. Arratia

Soils and sediments are soft, amorphous materials with complex microstructures and mechanical properties. They are also building blocks for industrial materials such as concrete. These Earth-mediated materials evolve under prolonged environmental pressures such as mechanical stress, chemical gradien…

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: Recent advances provide a coherent understanding of vacuum breakdown, which can inform the design of more reliable high-power technologies and advanced accelerators.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search channels, and project discovery potential for the High-Luminosity LHC based on current constraints.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC, but does not present new theoretical or experimental results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain scenarios, and the HL-LHC will have significant discovery potential across multiple channels.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental work from the last decade on nuclear reactions, plasma physics, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: It provides an updated understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning and its diagnostic probes.
conclusion: The paper advances solar model testing through improved nuclear reaction data and helioseismic constraints.

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.

method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, and multimodal approaches enhance its capabilities.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal systems expanding its applications.

This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: To understand strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding by studying charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: Highlights recent advances from BESIII, which has become the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The study of open-charm meson pairs provides valuable insights into QCD and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's planetary radar was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper is a historical review of radio astronomy achievements at the Arecibo Observatory, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo telescope in radio astronomy and related fields.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key observational results from Arecibo's five decades of operation.
result: Highlights major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave background detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades enabled sustained scientific impact across multiple areas of astronomy and atmospheric science.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science obtained with the Arecibo Observatory's radar, lidar, and optical instruments.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities enabled studies of ionospheric physics and space weather, but the paper focuses on atmospheric and plasma physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper is a review summarizing key results from incoherent scatter radar, lidar, and satellite-based observations of the upper atmosphere.
result: It highlights advances in understanding plasma physics, space weather, atomic metal layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace research, but the work is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers provide insights into turbulent fluctuations and supersaturation that help explain the precipitation bottleneck.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising platform for bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales to understand warm rain formation.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and gravitational waves provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents the latest modeling results and signal predictions, but does not introduce new results.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from core collapse supernovae, combined with photons and neutrinos, will enable multimessenger studies of the supernova central engine.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on large-scale structure surveys.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the matter distribution with the CMB dipole, which could reveal a fundamental inconsistency in the standard model of cosmology.
method: The authors analyze recent catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, comparing the observed dipole in their distribution with the CMB dipole, and review potential biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the ΛCDM model, but further investigation is needed to rule out systematic errors or alternative explanations.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark sector interactions and halo dynamics.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter by testing self-interaction models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures, comparing predictions of self-interacting dark matter models with data.
result: Summarizes current observational bounds on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and discusses implications for dark sector physics.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable hypothesis, with ongoing and future surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is a Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a classical machine learning model, with no direct connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper presents the Nobel lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, which are foundational to machine learning but not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The lecture describes the concept and training of Boltzmann machines, a type of stochastic recurrent neural network.
result: No new results; it is a retrospective overview of Boltzmann machines and their impact.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have been influential in machine learning, but the paper does not address quantum information theory or related fields.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper is a review summarizing key advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, including experimental and modeling approaches.
result: It highlights the effects of turbulence, non-Newtonian rheology, and surfactants on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or related fields.

Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory applied to buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth is important in materials science and biology.
